, lit. service (of the body), with special reference to (sexual) enjoyment: (kāya-pa˚); ˚ryā-saṃvarṇana commending of ‘service’ (Tib. bsñyen bkur), i.e. of sexual pleasure (in speaking to a woman; one of the saṃghāvaśeṣa sins); paricaryā (alone, in this sense). The Pali term is attakāmapāricariyā,, ministration to oneʼs lusts (). See also pāricaryā.

, nt., or ˚ṇā, f. (= Pali ˚ṇā; n. act. to next, mg. 1; in Skt. recorded only in mg. attendance; cf. AMg. pariyāraṇā, sexual pleasure), amusement (not necessarily sexual); only in ˚raṇārthaṃ, and only after krīḍārthaṃ ratyarthaṃ (cf. the grouping of the corresponding verbs, s.v. paricārayati; see also pravicāra, ˚cāraṇa or ˚ṇā):;.

(= Pali ˚reti, AMg. pariyārei; Skt. ˚rayate, only,, and, defined sich bedienen …, aufwarten lassen, but rather amuses oneself; cf.,, on, where it means … with women), (1) amuses oneself: very often preceded by krīḍati ramati (˚te), the latter sometimes omitted, as in; of any kind of amusement, as krīḍanakaiḥ krīḍanti ramanti paricārayanti, and so (not of sexual pleasures);;; (with liquor; read with mss. paricāretsu, proved by corresp. passage in Pali paricāresuṃ); but esp. of sexual enjoyment with women, krīḍāhi ramāhi paricārehi; similarly;;;;;; and often; etc.;; same trio of verbs but not clearly or exclusively of sexual pleasures (cf.);;;; (mss.);;; used alone, without krīḍ- and ram-, in the specific sense of has sexual intercourse (with, instr. with sārdhaṃ), Bhavena … tayā sārdhaṃ paricāritaṃ; tāḥ parapuruṣaiḥ sārdhaṃ paricārayanti; anayā parapuruṣeṇa sārdhaṃ paricāritaṃ, and similarly 2; ˚yati; ˚yāvaḥ, dual,; (2) attends, waits upon (a person; so simplex paricarati in Skt.): tena dāni pratyekabuddhena ye paricāritā (v.l. ˚vāritā) pratyekabuddhā(ḥ); sarve pi devasaṃghā devīṃ ( Māyāṃ) paricārayitva ākāśe = (vs), so in, in he reads ˚vārayitva (the mss. vary between these two both times); note that acc. to, Pali parivāreti is ‘often erroneously’ used for paricāreti; similarly, paricaritā (so read m.c. for paricārita, v.l. ˚vārita) purime nara ye te sarvasukhenā (vs), those men who formerly were attended (Tib. rim gro byas, made homage or offerings) by you with every joy; attends (a corpse, said of the funeral procession), paricārayitva (vs; no v.l.); ppp. attended, accompanied (of the mind), guṇagaṇa-paricārita-matī, his mind attended by flocks of good qualities; frequented, occupied (of a place), nairayikehi sattvehi śūlopetehi tāni parvatāni paricāritāni, these mountains are frequented by hell-inhabitants impaled on stakes (wrongly); (3) possibly to be read for paritārayanti in the mg. they get full knowledge of (cf. s.v. paritāraṇīya, where it is suggested that paricār˚ be read, to be sure not in this mg.); this is the regular Skt. mg. of pravicārayati, q.v., [Page322-b] which occurs in this mg. in the preceding line 10, and which in BHS is also used in the mg. of paricārayati (1), hence perhaps the latter may have come to be used also in the regular mg. of the former; but I have no parallel case; (4) summons (monks to a meeting): bhikṣūn paricārayitum ārabdhaḥ, so ms., ed. em. pracār˚; Tib. bsgrags pa, call.

, ppp. (essentially = Skt. and Pali id.), familiarized, well practised (in): ˚taḥ (supply vacasā, as in, see paricetar) = Tib. (yoṅs su, legs su, legs par, = pari) byaṅ ba, acc. to skilled; Pali vacasā paricita, in similar context,;. parijitaḥ; cf. parijaya.
(cf. Skt. cūrṇayati; the cpd. unrecorded), pulverizes completely: cakravāḍāḥ kacci sthiro (voc., = sthira in prec. line) me (used for acc. sg.) paricūrṇayeyuḥ (vs).
(cf. paricita), one who practises, is versed in (with instr.): vacasā ˚tā (v.l. ˚jitā; ˚jetā; cf. s.v. parijaya) = Tib. byaṅ ba, as for paricita, parijaya.

(Skt. id., in good sense, recites sacred formulae over; Pali id., recites magic spells, object vijjaṃ), recites magic charms over (with acc.), esp. of hostile or ‘black’ magic: mantraiḥ parijapto, bewitched; arkapuṣpaṃ parijapya; parijapya (object supplied).

, m. (see next; = Skt. paricaya,, cf. s.vv. paricita, paricetar), intensive cultivation, thorough acquaintance, familiarity, careful consideration (with loc.):; a-parijayād; prajñāyāṃ parijayaṃ karoṣi;; dhyāna-parijayaṃ ca karoti; ānimitte ca parijayaṃ karoti; śūnyatāyāṃ;. Prakritic j for c: cited by. According to, in the word would mean conquest, mastery, from root ji, and also in a ms. citation from Yaśomitra, (cf.) yogācāras trividhaḥ, ādikarmikaḥ, kṛtaparijayaḥ (un maître,), atikrāntamanasikāraś ca. I see no reason to separate these passages from the others. It is clear to me that BHS has only one word parijaya, and I think ʼs interpretation is the true one. Tib. on yoṅs su (= pari) byaṅ bar (sometimes purification, but also acc. to skilled; also used for paricita, ˚cetar, qq.v.; note that reads parijita, ˚jetar for these) byas pa (made, the making), or ḥdris par (acquaintance) bya ba (making, being made). Chin. and Jap. seem to follow Tib.

, prob. not masters, but the verb corresponding to parijaya, q.v., for Skt. paricaya: cultivates, considers carefully, gets well acquainted with: (bodhisattvavimokṣaṃ) bhāvayann avataran … parijayan paricintayan.

(= the more usual prati-jā˚), tends, cares for: sthānāni … parijāgriṣu (3 pl. aor.) (vs); (bodhisattvamātaraṃ devakanyā … ucchādana-)parimardanehi (or ˚mardana-,) pariṣekehi (so read, nearly with mss., see Crit. App.) pratijāgaranti = (prose).
, in ˚tāni puṣpāṇi, = Skt. pāri˚, a (heavenly) flower; not in, hence no doubt merely an uncorrected misprint for Skt. pāri˚.]
, var. for paricita, q.v., and cf. parijaya.

, adj. (= Skt. paridyūna; Pali parijunna,; cf. paridyāna; not *parijūrṇa, old, as assumed by,, and evidently), wretched, [Page323-a] miserable, poor; also parijūnya (nt., abstr. from prec.; once written in one ms. ˚juñña, in MIndic fashion), weakness, debility, poverty (Pali has the noun pārijuñña, nt.; the same four kinds as in are listed in; the Pkt. adj. parijuṇṇa, ˚junna, is defined by weak, poor, durbala, daridra, nirdhana, and doubtless belongs with this word): read in na … bodhisattvo jarāparijūnyena parijūno … abhiniṣkramati; in 17 … vyādhiparijūnyena (one ms. here ˚juññena) pari˚ …; in 19 … bhogapari˚ pari˚ …; in … jñātipari˚ pari˚ …; the mss. are corrupt in all these, but in 17 and 19 one of them is nearly right, reading ˚parijūtena parijūto or ˚parijūnena parijūno.
(nt.), weakness, poverty; see under prec. Should we read pārijūnya, with Pali pārijuñña ?
, var. for paricetar, q.v., and cf. parijaya.

(= Pali pariññā), (thorough) knowledge; here not used in any special or technical way: = Tib. yoṅs su śes pa; (nāmarūpa-pa˚); (vs, parijñācārī, read ˚jña˚ m.c. as in the same vs in Pali,, pariññacāri);;; (yathābhūta-parijñāyai);.

, ppp., distinguished, renowned:, ep. of the family into which the Bodhisattva is born in his last existence; must mean about the same as abhijñāta, which it follows; but omitted in the other versions of the same passage, and Cf. next two.

, adj. Bhvr. (= Pali pariññāta-bh˚), having true knowledge about food: pratyekabuddho pari˚ sarvāśuciparikṣīṇo mahābhāgo; ye ˚janā(ḥ) = Pali ye pariññātabhojanā, expl. in comm. as having the three pariññā, viz. ñāta-pa˚, knowing what the food is that he is eating; tīraṇa-pa˚, keeping in mind while eating that food is repulsive; and pahāna-pa˚, keeping in mind the rejection of pleasure in eating. I have found no evidence in BHS for this or any specific understanding of the term.
, adj. (= Pali pariññā˚; cf. Skt. parijñāta and), knowing thoroughly: (cyutyupapatti-)parijñātāvinaś ca.
= Skt. parijñāna, (state of) knowing; but perhaps rather analyze duḥkhaparijñāna plus -tā(yai):, unto a state of having thorough knowledge of misery.

, nt., or ˚nā, f., also ˚ṇa-tā (once Skt. ˚na in mg. transformation, changing into …; so also M.; not in Pali; cf. pariṇāmana, ˚nā, and Skt. pariṇamati), (1) change of state or occupation, in the sense of giving up one for another: pṛthivīsamacittena sarvabhāravahanāpariṇamana-tayā, with mind like the earth, in that it does not change (a-pari˚) from bearing all burdens; cited, where ed. as in text, but ms. aparitasyana-tayā (see this), in that it does not become wearied with …, which fits quite as well, tho presumably a secondary change; (2) ripening, maturing (in religious contexts): kuśalamūlānāṃ ˚nād; (bodhisattvasya) ˚nā; (the process consists in this, that … bodhisattvo … kuśalamūlaṃ … prasādena pariṇāmayati); ˚nā, the last of the seven anuttara-pūjā, supreme forms of worship, (following bodhicittotpādaḥ; probably understand bodhicittasya, or bodheḥ, with pari˚); sarvabodhisattvapariṇamanā-jñāna-; (sc. of Bodhisattvas) ˚nā; kuśalamūla-˚nā.
, nt. (= Skt. id., m.; also Pali; and cf. next), development, ripening, maturing: (sc. bodhisattva-)bhūmīnāṃ pariṇāmāni (vs).

, nt., or ˚nā, f. (cf. pariṇamana, ˚nā; Skt. pariṇamati, changes, intrans.; also ripens; Pali ˚na, only noted in mg. 4; AMg. ˚maṇā, ˚maṇayā for ˚manatā, transformation, change of form), (1) change, alteration: [Page323-b] priyavastu-pariṇāmana-tayā (because of the fact that there are alterations of the desired object) śokabhājano lābhasatkāraḥ; change of one physical element into another, mahābhūteṣv anyonya-pariṇāmanānyathābhāvakriyā; (2) ripening, lit., of a seed; (ṛtur api) bījasya pariṇāmanā-kṛtyaṃ karoti (Tib. bsgyur baḥi bya, see below), the act of causing the seed to ripen (or grow); (3) fig. development, causing to grow, ripening, maturation, usually of religiously desirable conditions; Tib. somewhat confused, sometimes yoṅs su (b)sṅo ba (so on and), said to mean regularly bless (certainly not the mg. of pariṇāmana); other mgs. cited are devote, design, intend; elsewhere (e.g.;) Tib. bsgyur ba, change, transform, but app. also multiply, increase, make grow; Chin. on turn, change (in direction): sarvā bodhisattvacaryāpagata-kleśakalmāṣā bodhipariṇāmanādhipatyena pratyetavyā(ḥ), all depravities and impurities foreign to the Bodhisattva-course are to be recognized, thru mastering the development (ripening) of enlightenment; bodhi-pariṇāmanā;; (prob. understand bodhi- also in) pariṇāmanakuśalena; prathamāyām eva pariṇāmanāyām, sc. of kuśalamūlāni; cf.; also pariṇāmanā; bodhisattva-˚nā-; imāya pariṇāmana-varṇitāya (vs), with this (sc. deśanā) which is praised as a cause of ripening; imaṃ ˚ṇa-rājaṃ, this King of Ripeners (the itself); yā pariṇāmana varṇita agrā; parahita-pariṇāmanāt, thru developing (increasing, furthering) the welfare of others; pariṇāmanaṃ, uncertain reading, replaced by pariṇamanā in line 8; iṣṭārthe pariṇāmanām; said of the development of an evil trait, (read) evam apsarasaḥ prārthanayābrahmacaryapariṇāmanān mahāpadumo nāma naraka uktaḥ, thus, as a result of the development (stimulation, ripening) of unchastity thru desiring an apsaras (wrongly); (4) (= Pali ˚naṃ,) diversion (of something to the use of someone for whom it was not intended): ˚nam.

, (1) (in Skt. and Pali recorded only as caus. to pariṇamati; acc. to, these BHS forms are denom. to pariṇāma; identical forms are also used, as in Skt. and Pali, in caus. sense, e.g.;; ʼs theory may be right; but cf.), = Skt. pariṇamati, ripens, matures, develops (intrans.): bodhisattvā avaivartikatāyai (or ˚ye) pariṇāmenti (prose), develop (themselves) towards …; pariṇāmayanto iha agrabodhau vayaṃ … (vs); pariṇāmayanti (with loc. of goal); (2) (= Pali ˚ṇāmeti; caus. to Skt. pariṇamati, is changed into) changes into: yo vārṣikaḥ (sc. lābhaḥ) sa haimantikaḥ pariṇāmitaḥ, yas tu haimantikaḥ sa vārṣikaḥ ˚mitaḥ; see s.v. saṃparivartayati; pariṇāmyamānaṃ, being changed, see s.v. svasti.

, m. (very rare in Skt.,, only in mg. 1; commoner in Pali, in both mgs.), (1) leader: ˚ka-saṃpannā, said of a herd of deer, perfect in their leader (who was Surūpa, a former birth of the Bodhisattva); as ep. of a Buddha, ˚kaḥ; mārga-˚kaḥ; andhe loke anāyake apariṇāyake Buddho … tārayitā etc., in a cliché,;;, etc.; ep. of Bodhisattvas, (loka-)˚kānāṃ; (sattvānāṃ …) pariṇāyakabhūtaḥ; (2) specifically, the 7th of the 7 ratna (q.v. 3) of a cakravartin: = Tib. blon po, officer, minister of state, app. with both civil and military functions of the highest rank under the king, so also Chin., while Jap. seems to make him more specifically military; same Tib. regularly elsewhere, e.g. on; for his functions, see, paṇḍito vyakto medhāvī rājñaś … cintitamātreṇa udyojayitavyaṃ (read surely ˚vyāṃ, as Tib. appears to take it, bsko bar bya baḥi dpuṅ rnams) senām udyojayati sma, he activates as quick as thought an [Page324-a] army that is to be activated for the king (here only military functions); suggests military functions; but contrariwise mārgagato praṇaṣṭānāṃ hatahatanayanānāṃ (read ˚nāna, m.c.) deśayati (so mss.) mārgaṃ, tena pariṇāyakavaraṃ labhati ratanaṃ (read ˚nam, m.c.; one ms. ratnam) uttamanāyakaṃ; for Pali cf. pariṇāyakaratanena vijitaṃ anurakkhati; paṭibalo rājānaṃ … upayāpetabbaṃ upayāpetuṃ apayāpetabbaṃ apayāpetuṃ ṭhapetabbaṃ ṭhapetuṃ, he is competent to bring to the king what needs to be brought, to remove what needs to be removed, to hold (make stay) what should be kept; comm., on this passage, says that he is the eldest son of the king, rañño jeṭṭhaputto va; a sort of viceroy or chief assistant to the king seems to be meant; very often in lists of the 7 ratna, without specific statement of his functions, e.g.;;;;;;;;;;;;;.

(nt.) or ˚ṇā, f. (cf. a-paritarṣaṇā, and Pali paritassanā), desire, longing: ˚ṇārthaṃ; ˚ṇārthena tṛṣṇā;; ˚ṇacittaṃ parivarjayitavyam;; ˚ṇā-cittam (with reference to a bhikṣuṇī; sexual desire). See also next, and paritṛṣita.

, nt. (prob. MIndic for ˚tṛṣ˚ to Pali paritasati, and esp. ˚tasita, ppp., see paritṛṣita), great longing, = utkaṇṭhā: tāṃs tathāgatān apaśyan (pres. pple.) mahatīm utkaṇṭhāṃ paritasanaṃ cāpannaḥ (prose), sc. to see the vision which had disappeared. Cf. also prec. The neg. a-paritasana, q.v., has been noted only as a noun from the different verb parit(r)as(y)ati; in Pali the two seem to be confused, at least if the are to be trusted. It must be noted, however, that the meaning discouragement, mental trouble (as in a-paritasyana etc., cf. paritasyati, ˚tras˚) would be possible in the above passage, and could also be the meaning of utkaṇṭhā, as in Pali ukkaṇṭhā and BHS utkaṇṭhati; the disappearance of the vision could lead to depression of mind, as well as to eager desire to see it again.

(= paritrasyati, ˚sati; Pali paritassati, ˚tasati, which seems to be blended with derivs. of Skt. tṛṣ-; cf. (na) paritassati; comm. glosses, bhaya-paritassanāya taṇhā-paritasanāya vā na paritassati, is not disturbed either by fear (?) of danger or desire(?) for cravings, distinguishing the two nouns paritassanā and ˚tasanā but associating both with the verb paritassati; the forms with -tras- may indicate the true origin, or may be hyper-Skt., association with root trasbeing then secondary; cf. tas = upakṣaye, but with var. upakṣepe), is wearied, exhausted, troubled, disturbed; cf. paritasyati, upakṣīyata ity arthaḥ (see s.v. paritāsa): na ˚syati (ed. adds, as variant?, paritrasyati; ˚tas˚ without v.l.; follows parikhedaḥ; forms related to this word occur with other forms mentioned in this article) = Tib. yoṅs su (= pari) mi (= na) (ḥ) chad = decay, cease; so Chin. and Jap.; notkaṇṭhyate (see utkaṇṭhati) na ˚syati; a-paritasyamānaḥ. Cf. a-paritasyana(tā), and; ʼs theory there cited seems hardly conclusive.
(nt.; = Pali id.), (self-)torture (in ascetic practices), esp. in cpd. ātāpana-pari˚, see s.v. ātāpana; also kāyaparitāpanārthaṃ.
, gdve. ˚tāyitavya (MIndic, to Skt. ˚trāyate), saves, rescues: paritāyitavya maya sattva duḥkhārditāni (read dukhā˚).
, m. (nom. act. to paritasyati), troubled mental state, discouragement: paritāso daurmanasyam, tena hi paritasyate, upakṣīyata ity arthaḥ.

(nt.; except in could also be understood as ˚nā, f.; n. act. to next; not recorded), also ˚na-tā, weighing (mentally), consideration: -doṣa-paritulanākāraṃ (sc. of śruta); śrutārtha-˚na-tā; ˚nābhimānatā; ˚nāsaṃmoha-(asaṃmoha-); ˚na-.
(= Pali ˚tuleti; cf. prec.), weighs (mentally), considers: ˚yati (ātmānaṃ); ˚yataḥ, gen. sg. pres. pple., (svārthaṃ); ˚yamānena, pres. pple. mid.,; ˚yitvā (antaḥpuraṃ).

, adj. (ppp. of next, q.v.; = Pali ˚tasita, presumably subst., extreme craving, in taṇhāgatānaṃ paritasita-vipphanditam eva; see paritasana, and ˚tarṣaṇa, ˚ṇā; Skt. has no form of pari plus tṛṣ-, but the ppp. of tṛṣyati is Skt. tṛṣita; in Pali there seems to be great confusion between forms of this root in -s-, based chiefly on tṛṣita, leading even to a present tasati, and in -ss-, based partly on tṛṣyati, partly on Skt. fullgrade forms in tarṣ-; in, above, the v.l. ˚tassita is recorded in text and comm.; both these are moreover confused in Pali with the homonyms related to BHS paritasyati, ˚tras(y)ati), eagerly desirous, longing, with dat. or instr. or preceding stem in comp.: ˚tāḥ smo bhagavato darśanāya ( ˚nena);; darśana-pari˚;; dharma-pari˚; (absolute use).
(see prec.; Pali paritassati beside ˚tasati), longs eagerly for, with gen.: sa tasyāḥ (sc. sukhāyā vedanāyāḥ) punaḥ-punaḥ saṃyogārthaṃ ˚te (prose).

, adj. (= Pali id., = parītta, q.v.), small: (so with all mss.); (read parittaṃ for text pariktaṃ or, with dittography, pariktaktaṃ; separate from the preceding word, see abhyantarita; Tib. chuṅ ba, little).
, ppp. (Pali pariccatta; cf. s.v. tyaj with pari, 5; cited only Gr.), (food that is) left over: yadi (or, sacet) te (bhagini) ˚ktam ākīryatām (or, dīyatām) asmin pātre;; (in a modest request).
(nt.; = Pali pariccajana), giving up, giving away: -lokadhātoḥ ˚naṃ (syntax not clear; there seems to be no verb in the sentence as printed).

(looks like cpd. of pari plus Skt. trasyati, trasati, cf. Skt. ppp. paritrasta; but equivalent to paritasyati, q.v.; Pali usually paritassati, ˚tasati, but occasionally paritt˚, as in parittase, cf. parittāsin), = paritasyati, and used in similar contexts: na paritrasyati (in same line na parikhidyate, cf. parikhedaḥ, and see s.v. paritasyati; in next line nāvasīdati); (na parikhidyante na saṃsīdanti … na) paritrasyanti; na paritrasanti (parallel na parikhidyante, line 20).
, m. (= Pali parittāyaka; to Skt. ˚trāyate plus -aka), rescuer: ˚kā mama kalyāṇamitrāḥ (prose).
(nt.; n. act. to Skt. ˚trāyate plus -ana; cf. Skt. paritrāṇa, Pali parittāṇa), rescuing, saving: sattva- ˚ṇārthaṃ (vs); jagat-˚ṇārthāḥ; sarvasattvadhātu-˚ṇena (prose).

(pass. to Skt. paridahati, which seems recorded only in lit. sense, burns; Pali pariḍayhati, subject cittaṃ,), is tormented (with passion or desire; cf. paridāha etc.): rāgeṇa ˚hyāmi; āhāratṛṣṇā-˚hyamānāḥ.

, m. (nowhere recorded; cf. next; Pali pariḷāha in all mgs.), (1) hot weather: ˚gha-samayaḥ (not noted in this sense in, but found in pariḷāha-samaye); (2) ardent desire (Pali kāma-pariḷāho), kāma-paridāghā, Bhvr., having an ardent desire for lusts,; read ˚ghaḥ in with ms. for text pradāśaḥ; vimuktaḥ paridāghaiḥ, said of a Tathāgata, perhaps rather to mg. 3; Tib. yoṅs su gduṅ ba, which is equally ambiguous, having the same two mgs.; (3) torment, anguish: antaḥśalyaparidāgha-jāta, see s.v. antaḥśalya; śokaśalya-paridāghaṃ (acc.); rūpa-(or, in 8, vijñāna-)-pratyayā … paridāghā; jvara-˚ghaḥ; dvau … ˚ghau (text ˚gho) (Tib. as on above; parallels vraṇa in and glānya indicate this mg. rather than 2).

, m. (Skt. only lit. burning, and fig. mental anguish; = Pali pariḷāha; cf. paridahyati, paridāgha, and niṣparidāha), (1) fever (disease):, in list of diseases, Tib. tsha ba, heat; (2) feverish longing, ardent desire, substantially = tṛṣṇā, as a vice: kāmeṣu ˚haḥ; in lists of vices,;;.

(? nt.), ˚na-tā, ˚nā, f. (= Pali ˚na, ˚nā; n. act. to next; clear cases of ˚na, nt., not recorded, prob. by accident), explanation, clarification, expounding, setting forth: (sattva-)˚nā kṛtā; sarvasaṃsāranityatvaparidīpanatāyai; ˚panān, ifc. Bhvr.,; ˚panākāraṃ, Bhvr.,

(ppp. to caus. of ˚padyati, q.v.), completely developed or accomplished: bodhisattvacaryā (so divide)˚ditā; asmābhiḥ sarvabuddhadharmāḥ ˚ditāḥ; ˚ditāḥ sarvasamādhayaḥ; na ca mayaikasattvasyārthe ātmabhāvaḥ pariniṣpāditaḥ (misprinted), and I have not developed (formed; zur Erscheinung bringen, offenbaren, not quite accurately) a (material) body for the sake of a single creature (Avalokiteśvara speaks).
(also parī˚; to parindāmi), the giving over, presenting: ˚nārthaṃ; ˚nayā; (prose, not vs); see s.v. parīndanā on.

(also parī˚, anu-par˚, qq.v.; peculiar to BHS; formation unexplained, see below), I present, hand over: ˚āmi;; (paridāmy, read with v.l. parind˚); ppp. parindita, see Parinditārtha, and, where parindita is read for parī˚. Could nasalized vowel -in- (-iṃ) be a substitute by the ‘law of Morae’ for parī-dāmi (cf. ppp. parītta), and the forms with parīnd˚ be blends? Not satisfactory. But parī- occurs for pari-. would derive by the Morengesetz from *pariddāmi for paridadāmi with loss of -a-; as a parallel he cites Skt. ujjhāmi etc., which he also derives directly from uj-jahāmi with loss of -a-. That ujjh- is somehow derived from ud plus root hā, few will doubt; but I am not sure that this is the precise way (for a different one see s.v.); and I should like other examples of such loss of -a-.
(cf. prec. items), n. of a former Buddha:.

, in (prose) suparipaṇḍitaśukla-dharmāṇo,, but v.l. ˚paripiṇḍita˚, supported by Tib. bsdus pa, accumulated, and proved by the same cpd.; see paripiṇḍayati.]

, f. ˚ikā, adj. (to ˚pācayati plus -aka), bringing to maturity (in religious sense): ˚kāḥ pudgalāḥ; (kalyāṇamitrāṇi …) samyaksaṃbodhau … ˚cakāni; jñāna-˚kair dharmaiḥ; bodhi-˚cikā … devata (= ˚tā) (vs).

I have no exact parallel to this usage but can conceive no other interpretation; ʼs is very unsatisfactory (and involves the most implausible em. sāgare).

, ppp.,, enjoyed, utilized, as in Skt.: te [sc. vihārāḥ; follows phrase cited s.v. niryātayati; misunderstands the reference of the pronoun] ca mayā ˚tā veditavyāḥ, and these [monasteries] are to be regarded as having been utilized by me; cf. mayā sa bhuktaḥ pṛthivīpradeśo.)
, adj. (= Skt. ˚kta), utilized; specifically, worn, used (of a garment): (vastraṃ).
(m. or nt.), a high number:. Corresp. to haribha, nt., q.v.

, m. (commonly, as in Skt. and Pali, enjoyment, usufruct, use, also article of enjoyment; e.g. bodhisattvasya paribhogārtham, ˚gāya 16), property to be enjoyed, in … ratnavyūhaṃ bodhisattvaparibhogaṃ draṣṭuṃ yo mātuḥ kukṣigatasya bodhisattvasya paribhogo 'bhūt, refers to a physical (tho of course magical) structure, described in detail, which houses the Bodhisattva in his motherʼs womb; it had three turrets or apartments, kūṭāgāra, one within the other, and within the third a couch or litter, paryaṅka; it was hard ‘like vajra’ yet soft to the touch (); all the bhavana-vyūha of the kāmāvacara gods appeared in it (); it always develops or appears in the right side of a Bodhisattvaʼs mother in his last earthly existence (, here called ratnavyūhaḥ, q.v., kūṭāgāro); in referred to again, drakṣasi (so text and app. all mss.) tvam Ānanda ratnavyūhaṃ bodhisattvaparibhogaṃ yatra bodhisattvo mātuḥ kukṣigato vyāhārṣīt. Tib. on renders literally, complete enjoyment, yoṅs su spyad pa, cf. paribhogaḥ = Tib. yoṅs su spyod.. kūṭāgāraparibhogeṣu cātra bodhisattvān nivasato drakṣyati, [Page328-b] does not refer to this magical structure in the womb, but to structures occupied by bodhisattvas while attending on the Buddha Śākyamuni.
, adj. (cf. next two), usable, fit for use: sati ˚gīye (vv.ll. ˚gike, pāribhogīye) pātre ūnapañcabandhane. But pari˚ seems to be lacking in Chin., acc. to, and is lacking in the Pali,.
(cf. prec. and next), (1) adj., usable, fit for use, suitable, salutary: pānīyaṃ ˚gyaṃ; (2) subst. (nt.), use: puṣkariṇyo jala-paribhogya-sthās; bhaiṣajya-śarāva-˚gyena paribhoktavyāni.
, adj. or subst. nt., useful (object, sc. for monks): sarvaṃ ˚jyaṃ.
, adj., read pārima, q.v. (not Pali parima = Skt. parama, supreme, highest), further (with tīra, bank): (prose) ˚ma-tīra-gāminī.]

, adj. (corresp. to Pali parimāṇa, as adj., etc.), f. ˚vatī (āpatti), (sin) of (definite) extent (?):, etc.; opp. a-parimāṇavatī; (= Pali aparimāṇa). The real mg. is not clear, nor is it clear which category is more serious. Pali is equally uncertain, see. It does not mean ‘if the period is known’ (), for the period (rātriparyanta) may be known or unknown in the case of an aparimāṇavatī,
, adj., and ˚ṇā, subst. (Skt. only ˚ṇa, nt., subst. = BHS ˚ṇā), (1) adj., searching: ˚ṇaḥ paripṛcchan; (2) subst., (act of) searching: (kalyāṇamitra-)˚ṇāsu.
(= Pali ˚majjaka), touching, attaining to: candrama-sūrya-˚jako maharddhiko … ṛṣi, who (by magic) can travel to the moon and sun; so Pali canda-suriya-parimajjaka.
(to prec.; = Pali parivīmaṃsā), investigation, careful consideration:; etc.
, adj. or subst. (to ˚cayati), saving, one who saves: saṃsāraduḥkha-pa˚.

, nt. (to next; cited by without reference; AMg. ˚moyaṇa acc. to), saving, salvation, freeing, either from the saṃsāra etc. (religiously), or in ordinary worldly application:;;;;;;;; kleśavyādhi-˚na-tayā, because he saves from …

(= Pali ˚moceti; in Skt. only non-caus. ˚muñcati), saves, rescues (usually but not invariably in religious sense, cf. ˚mocana): ˚caya; ˚cayeyaṃ; ˚cayasva; active finite forms,;;;;; ger. ˚cya; ˚cayitvā (prose); gdve. ˚cayitavya;; inf. ˚cayitu-kāma; ppp. ˚cita;;
(to prec.), one who frees: ˚tāro 'jñānagahanāt (so read with 2d ed. for 1st ed. jñāna˚).
(nt.; n. act. to *pari plus mrakṣ-), smearing, rubbing on: -pāṃśu-paṅka-˚ṇaiś ca (prose).
, m. (= Pali id., Skt. paryanta), end, limit: parvatacakravāḍa-pariyantāḥ (so text, acc. pl. m.; … āvasati sarvān) (vs).
(m.; to the very rare Skt. pari-labh-), acquisition: sudurlabha-buddharatna-parilābha- (prose).

, adj. or ppp. (perhaps really cpd. of pari, intensive, and vandita; Skt. has pari-vand only once in; but cf. AMg. parivandijjamāṇa, pres. pass. pple., and n. act. parivandaṇa), highly praised: naramaru- ˚ditaṃ sugataṃ (vs).
, ppp. (cf. Pali vambheti), acc. to, v.l. of of for Nep. parivañcita. Cf. nirvamhaṇa.
(= Pali id., both; Skt. only ˚na, nt.), avoidance: caturvāgdoṣa-˚natāyai; mātsarya-˚natā; pāpamitra-˚nā (all prose).

, in yo (mss. ye) evarūpaṃ (mss. ˚pena) naradamyasārathi (em. ˚thiṃ) dṛṣṭvā maharṣiṃ parivarjayeyaṃ (em. ˚ya), hastehi pādehi ca so mahāśiriṃ praṇāmaye … (vs) acc. to satisfaire, rendre favorable (= ā-varj-); but I find it hard to believe that it could mean anything else than avoid. Should we read something like parivārayeya (or paricār˚), would wait upon? This would at least make good sense.

(= Pali ˚vaṇṇayati; Skt. ppp. ˚varṇita, described), extols, describes with laudation: yaṃ buddhaśreṣṭho ˚ṇaye (aor., or opt.?) śuciṃ (vs) = Pali yaṃ buddhaseṭṭho parivaṇṇayī (comm. pasaṃsi pakāsayi, aor.) suciṃ.

, m. (in mg. 2 rarely nt.; in mg. 1 = Pali parivaṭṭa), (1) turn, revolution (so in Skt.): ekasmi cittaparivarti (vs), in a single turn of thought (= in one instant); substantially = method, process, ime punaḥ pañca dharmāḥ (= bodhisattvaliṅgāni, line 4, cf. pañca bodhisattvaliṅgāni pañcaparivartena veditavyāni) pañcaparivartena veditavyāḥ; esp. applied to one of the three ‘turns’ of the ‘wheel of the law’ or stages in development of knowledge of the four noble truths; they are most clearly stated in beginning āryasatyānāṃ prathamaparivarto darśanamārgaḥ, the first turn … is the way of seeing, sc. what the 4 truths are; these are stated; … dvitīyaparivarto bhāvanāmārgaḥ, … the way of putting them into effect, viz. as stated in, duḥkham āryasatyaṃ parijñeyam, duḥkhasamudayaḥ prahātavyaḥ, duḥkhanirodhaḥ sākṣātkartavyaḥ, duḥkhanirodhagāminī pratipad bhāvayitavyā; āryasatyānāṃ tṛtīyaḥ parivarto 'śaikṣamārgaḥ (so Tib. mi slob paḥi lam), the stage in which the efforts of the 2d stage have succeeded, duḥkhaṃ parijñātam, samudayaḥ prahīnaḥ, nirodhaḥ sākṣātkṛtaḥ, duḥkhanirodhagāminī pratipad bhāvitā. Similarly Similar (but somewhat less clear) detailed statements in (here the last two parts of the 2d parivarta and the first two of the 3d are omitted, by accident or compression), and in Pali (here all is stated, but the three parivarta as relating to each of the four noble truths are each compressed into a single statement). The whole is referred to in as triparivartaṃ dvādaśākāraṃ (because each parivarta refers to each of the four truths) jñānadarśanam, and similarly (omitting jñānadarśanaṃ; trip˚ and dvād˚ seemingly adverbs, the noun is āryasatyāni); Pali tiparivaṭṭaṃ dvādasākāraṃ … ñāṇadassanaṃ. With reference to this, the dharmacakra is called triparivarta (usually also dvādaśākāra); (vs);;; (2) m. or (rarely) nt., (orig. turn,) section, part, chapter of a literary work; ˚taṃ (acc.); asmin … dharmālokamukhaparivarte, here section, not one of the formal chapters of the work, and so; parivartān, chapters; ˚taḥ = Tib. le ḥu, section, chapter; regularly in the colophons [Page329-b] of various works, m. in,,,, parīndanā-parivarto (read as one word), cf. dharmamukhaparivarto, in body of text; nt. ˚taṃ (colophon); I have failed to note the word elsewhere in colophons of; idaṃ saddharmapuṇḍarīkasūtraparivartaṃ (so with) śroṣyati (prose; acc.); (3) m. or nt., math., square (of a number): (after asaṃkhyeyam) asaṃkhyeya-parivartaḥ (Tib. bsgres pa, multiply,); and so in etc., and in the similar table of large numbers (cited from);; (which last makes the mg. unmistakable; e.g. aparimāṇam aparimāṇānām aparimāṇaparivartam).
, m. or nt. (= ˚ta, 2), chapter, section (of a work): prathame ˚take (referring to what?).

(= Pali ˚vattati; in Skt. without complement, changes), (1) changes into (with nom.): = Pali, which proves ʼs text wrong; read, nadīm upemi (so one ms.; most mss. upeti, upenti) tṛṣitā, riktikā (mss. ˚kāṃ) parivartati (it is changed so as to be empty); chāyām upemi (mss. ˚ti) saṃtaptā, ātapo parivartati (it changes to sunshine); (2) like Skt. pariṇamati, (changes, then) develops, ripens, matures: ye caivaṃ parivartantā (most mss. ˚tentā, perh. read so, but not in caus. mg.) na vivartanti paṇḍitāḥ (vs), who are thus maturing … (otherwise).
(nt.? to Skt. parivartati; not recorded precisely in this sense), turning-place, place of habitual movement, in golāṅgula-p˚, q.v.
, v.l. ˚vartatā, in cakṣuḥ-pari˚, rolling (of the eyes): instr. ˚ayā,.
, adj. (to Skt. and Pali ˚vahati), carrying around: hayanavarehi ˚vahī (mātāpitaraṃ … rājā) (vs).
, adj. or subst. m. (cf. Skt. ˚vāda), reviling, one who reviles: asmākaṃ ˚kāḥ (vs).
(so, or parivānī, mss.; = Skt. ˚vādinī, so em., perhaps rightly; ˚vādinī, no real v.l.,), a seven-stringed lute: ˚nīyo, n. pl.,.
, nt. (= Pali ˚ra, m., title of the Appendix to,, colophon), accessory (text), appendix, addendum: avalokitaṃ nāma sūtraṃ mahāvastusya parivāraṃ, colophon to second version of the Avalokita sūtra.

(Skt. has ppp. ˚vārita; Pali ˚vāreti, regarded by as error for ˚cāreti, but may easily be denom. from Skt. parivāra, retinue), attends, waits upon (with gen.?): tasyā (mss. tasya) … parivāresi (aor.; but mss. ˚retvā); note on says mss. of ‘sometimes’ read parivārayati for paricār˚.

, m. (Skt., period of residence; = Pali id. in technical sense), period of probation to which certain monks were subjected, as a disciplinary measure, for concealment of a saṃghāvaśeṣa offense: ˚saḥ; mūla-pari˚; mūlāpakarṣa-pari˚ (on these see s.v. mūla); same three;; Tib. spo ba, change, esp. of residence. Its extent was equal to the period of concealment. See next, and 1 paryuṣita- (parivāsa). In passim; origin and prescription of the three varieties, as in, (in the pārivāsika-vastu).

, in paryuṣita-pari˚, seems equivalent to parivāsa, q.v.: paryuṣita-parivāsitena bhikṣuṇā, by a monk who has completed his period of probation; the Pali is parivuttha-(or ˚ṭṭha-)-parivāsa, see 1 paryuṣita.

(= Pali id.,; cf. Skt. parivāsa, 2,), perfumed: sugandhi-(v.l. ˚dha-)-tailapari˚; divyagandha-pari˚;; [Page330-a] in assoc. with vāsanā, q.v., prob. means something like conditioned, habituated, and if connected with our word, used only in fig. sense (so Jap. understands it, but not Tib. or Chin.; I do not understand the Tib. renderings, yoṅs su bskos pa or bgos pa, the latter clothed, suggesting association with root vas, dress).

, adj. or subst. m. (no cpd. of pari-vijñā recorded), making (one who makes) completely known: trisahasra ājña-parivijñapanī (n. or voc. sg.; short a may be m.c., cf. Pali viññāpana; v.l. ˚jñāpana, unmetr. in antepenult and ultima) jagasya, kṣipraṃ pramuñca bhagavan mahabuddhaghoṣaṃ (—20; vs).

, m., rarely nt. (= Pali ˚takka), reflection, consideration, thought: tasyāsi ˚ko (vs), he reflected; almost always, as in Pali, preceded by cetaḥ- (always in comp. with pari˚, tho sometimes printed separately in edd.), or gen. cetasaḥ; eva(ṃ)rūpaś (˚po) cetaso parivitarka udapādi (also ˚pāsi, utpadye, aor.);;;;;; same but with cetasi cetaḥparivitarka (˚kam) udapādi;;; evaṃrūpaś cetasaḥ (v.l. cetasaiva cetaḥ-)˚tarka utpannaḥ; of someone, regularly Buddha, ‘recognizing’ the mental processes of others by his own mind, cetasaiva cetaḥparivitarkam ājñāya (very common, e.g.);;;;;;;; (read with best ms. A, text tr. cetaś cetasaiva pari˚);; cetaso parivitarkam ājñāya;;;;; with pl. subject, cetobhir (for cetasā) …; with aor. ājñāsīt (for ājñāya); evaṃrūpeṇa (adv.; sc. cetasā ? but this adj. does not otherwise occur in this phrase and is prob. introduced by confusion with the phrase cited previously) cetaḥpari˚ ājñāya; ākāra-pari˚ (= Pali ākāra-parivitakka), careful consideration of appearances (or conditions),.
, adj. or ppp. (prob. not ppp. to Vedic pari-vid, but noun cpd. of pari, intens., with Skt. vidita), well known:.
(= AMg. parivisiṭṭha), especial, particular: pariviśiṣṭān āveṇikān (sc. dharmān). Prob. n. cpd. of pari, intens., plus viśiṣṭa.
, adj. or ppp. (prob. n. cpd. of pari plus ppp. viśuddha), completely purified: triguṇa-pari˚.

, also written ˚sati in mss. (= Pali ˚visati; Epic Skt. ˚veṣati and AMg. ˚vesai), serves with food: ˚ṣati (to be read for mss. parivasati or prativas˚, em. praticarati);;; opt. ˚viṣeyaṃ; ger. ˚viṣitvā (mss. ˚śitvā, em. ˚sitvā); (mss. ˚śitvā, here ˚ṣitvā); fut. ˚viṣiṣyāmaḥ; pass. ˚viṣīyati.
(Pali so cited by without reference; ppp. ˚ṭhita in; MIndic for Skt. ˚veṣṭayati), wraps up: ˚ṭhitvā (taṃ bhūrjaṃ kāṇḍe, mss. kaṇṭho, kaṃtho);; ˚ṭhitaṃ (mss. ˚veṭ˚, ˚veṣṭ˚).

(= Pali id.), cell, apartment (of a monk or nun); only by ʼs em., sā parivrājikā upadarśitā svake ˚ṇe … svādhyāyaṃ karontī. Both mss. purimante, or (omitting svake) ˚tena, for pariveṇe; prob. a form of purima, q.v., is contained here; perhaps purimaṃ, adv., in front, before him, foll. by tena (with foll. svareṇa).]
(cf. Pkt. parivellira, defined kampana śīla; to Skt. root vell), makes wavering: ˚yiṣyanti (cittāni). Cf. next (?).

, ger.? (or ˚valliya?), in = kusumalatā va drumavaraṃ śayanaṃ parivelliyā (mss. ˚ya, ˚valliya; ˚yā, required by meter) śayitā, perh. embracing: she lay hugging the couch as a [Page330-b] flowering creeper (embraces) an excellent tree. It is uncertain whether the root vell or (chiefly) vall should be recognized. prints as if cpd. with śayitā and interprets otherwise.
, adj. (= Pali ˚vyatta; pari, intensive, plus vyakta), very clear, distinct: ˚tenākṣarapadavyañjanena.

, m. (= Pali paribbaya), allowance for (daily) expenses: (divasa-pari˚) and ff.;;; fig. bāṣpa-parivyayena, with spending (lavish pouring forth) of tears. Cf. pārivyayika. (In = Tib. spod, spice, as in Skt.,.)
, adj. (pari, intensive, plus vyā˚), completely confused, disordered:; ˚lī-kṛta, made …,.
(= Pali ˚saṅkā; to Skt. pari-śaṅk-), suspicion:; dṛṣṭena śrutena ˚kayā vā.
, app. nearly = śara, dart, arrow: śokapariśara-viddha-(mss. ˚ddho) hṛdayo (prose). Should we read by transposition śoka-śara-parividdha-?
, adj. (pari, intensive, plus śi˚), very loose or lax:; ˚la-śirāsthicarmagātra.

, f., seems to me used in no different mg. from purification, purity, = Skt. id., Pali ˚suddhi; so even in maṇḍala-pariśuddhiṃ kathaṃ saṃjānīte, where renders richtige Beschaffenheit, Correctheit. A few other passages:;;.)
, adj. (to Skt. BHS ˚śodhayati, Pali ˚sodheti, purifies), purifying: ˚kaḥ; bodhicaryā˚kā dharmāḥ (here misprinted pāri˚), 12; bhūmi- ˚kān dharmān (cf. pariśodhika).
, adj. (= ˚dhaka; perhaps wrong reading for that), purifying: bhūmi-˚kāni.
, (1) n. of an apsaras:; (2) n. of a ‘gandharva maid’:.

, em. in, where mss. unmetrically gṛha-dhana-(em. m.c. gṛhe dhane)-putrabhārya-pariśuddhaḥ or ˚dhaṃ; Tib. for the last member chags, devoted, attached, fond; no pari-śrad-dhā is recorded, and the em. seems implausible, but the mss. reading can hardly be right. The best em. that has occurred to me is pariṣaktāḥ, to Skt. pari-sajjate; see pariṣakta for another possible occurrence.]
, nt. (= Pali parissaya), (obstacle?) difficulty, danger: abhibhūya sarvāṇi pariśrayāṇi (= Pali parissayāni). See parisrava.
, attached, enmeshed, involved, prob. to be read for pariṣikta(m idaṃ kalipāśa jagat), cited (entangled; Tib. thogs, hindered, which elsewhere translates derivs. of root sañj). See s.v. pariśraddhāḥ.

(once written ˚khaṇḍa), (1) m., or ˚ḍā, f., acc. to Tib. (baṅ rim) terraced approach, flight of steps (leading to a mountain, usually Sumeru, or to a building, acc. to a chorten, i.e. stūpa): ˚ḍaḥ; dvārakoṣṭhake ˚ḍāyāṃ caṅkrameṣu; most often Sumeru- (pariṣaṇḍaḥ);; (˚khaṇḍaṃ, acc.); ˚pariṣaṇḍāyāṃ, loc. f.,;;; pariṣaṇḍo tadā Mero(r) (vs); pariṣaṇḍa-vārika, m. (see vārika),, (monk) in charge of the flight of steps (to a building, no doubt a stūpa); (2) m., ˚ḍaḥ, 9 ˚ḍa-cīvareṇa, perh. corruption for Pali paribhaṇḍa, which [Page331-a] renders binding along the back (of a robe); Tib. zegs pa (? zegs ma = dirt,, water-spray,).
, m. (Skt. Lex.) = pāri˚, q.v.: amātyapari˚ (mss., em. -pāri˚) (prose).

(also parṣā and rarely parṣadā, qq.v.;; = Pali parisā, Skt. pariṣad and parṣad), assembly: in prose of acc. to ˚ṣāyaḥ (abl.-gen.), instead of parṣadi (loc.) of; ˚ṣāya (gen.) (vs); ˚ṣāṃ (māra-); (naramaru-; both vss); in prose,;;;;;;; catuhi pariṣāhi (of a Buddha, viz. monks, nuns, male and female upāsakas, as in Pali); vss, (meter bad, ˚ṣāyāṃ, but ʼs suggestion parṣadi requires further change to correct it);.

(nt.; n. act. to Skt. pariṣiñcati; = Skt. pariṣecana), sprinkling: -pravrajita- … -sugandhatailamūrdhni-˚naṃ (nt. acc. adv., or n. sg. of separate statement ?) sarvayācanakebhyaś cūrṇamālya- … -pradānatvād.

, m. (also pariskāra; = Pali parikkhāra), equipment, utensils, personal belongings: = Tib. yo byad;; ˚ra-vaśitā, one of the 10 vaśitā of a Bodhisattva,;; ˚ra-cīvaram, presumably the robe as part of (a monkʼs) standard belongings; not of a monk but of an ordinary (poor) man,; often in a standard list, (a monkʼs) cīvarapiṇḍapāta-(or ˚tra-)-śayanāsana-glānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkāra (or ˚skāra; same in MIndic form in Pali, counted as four items),;;;;;;;;; (and same list without the word pariṣkāra);;;;; elsewhere without list, referring to anything which could properly be given to a monk,; six pariṣkāra (of a monk),, not listed (it is hard to see how the above list could count up to six; perhaps the ‘eight’ listed s.v. parikkhāra are meant, the three robes counting as one item); āgṛhīta-pari˚, see āgṛhīta; doubtful is pariṣkāra-vigata-malāmātsarya-sunigṛhītacitta, where renders implausibly ‘etwa an sich geübte Zucht’; must have read susaṃgṛhīta-puṇyapariṣkāraḥ, as part of the preceding word, assuming mg. parure (as in Skt.); Tib. omitted in; saptasamādhi-pariṣkāra- (dāyaka, of Buddhas), explained by Pali, the seven pari˚ (comm. gloss paricārikā, v.l. parivārikā) are the first seven stages of the noble 8-fold path, because they lead progressively to the eighth stage, sammā-(samyak-)samādhi; the word here seems to mean utensils in the sense of means leading towards (l. c. sammāsamādhissa bhāvanāya samādhissa pāripūriyā). In; (bheda-)pariṣkāra (tho rendered in Tib. yo byad!) is false Skt. for Pali (bheda-)purekkhāra.

, adj. (to prec. plus -ika; Pali parikkhārika recorded only as one possessing the p.), belonging to the personal belongings (of a monk): mṛta-˚ka (in 20 quasi-subst., what belongs …); (with prativastu).

, ppp., in su-pari˚, app. used in sense of Skt. pratiṣṭhita, Pali patiṭṭhita, with confusion of MIndic paṭi (pati, = prati) and pari,, (well) established (or, acc. to Tib., properly taught? gnas par bstan): ˚tā (spelled ˚sthitā) sā varabuddhabodhis (vs); parallel with darśitā in 7.
, m. (to ˚ṣyandayati; unrecorded in this sense), moisture: = Tib. rlon pa, brlan pa, gśer ba.
(nt.; to next; cf. prec.), saturation (fig.): asmimāna-˚na-taḥ.

(= Pali parisandeti), = abhiṣyandayati, q.v., which often precedes it, as in Pali; saturates, irrigates, moistens: literally (plants); of the mind (citta), kuśalamūlaiḥ svacittam eva pariṣyandayitavyam; manasikāra-pariṣyanditena cittena; as a yoga-practice, after abhiṣyand˚,.
(nt.; n. act. to caus. of pari plus svid, used in Suśruta,), sweating (as a form of medical treatment): ˚danam (… prajānāmi), in list of methods of treating diseases.

, adj.-ppp. (cf. Skt. pari-sam-stu-, praise, once in,), in (bodhisattvāḥ …) tathāgata- ˚tā(ḥ), either praised by … (so Tib. and later Chin.), or intimate with … (cf. saṃstuta; so earliest Chin., Dharmarakṣa).

, and (perhaps only m.c.) ˚sthapeti (cf. next; caus. of pari-saṃ-sthā-, not recorded Skt. or Pali; cf. Pkt. parisaṃṭhaviṃta, ˚ṭhaviya), establishes, fixes, makes firm, arranges in fixed order: ˚sthāpayati (buddhakṣetra); (lokadhātu); ˚sthāpayāmi (parivartān, chapters or sections of a literary work); ˚sthapemi (vs, perhaps m.c.; yuṣmān, followers of Buddha); ˚sthāpayiṣyati (puṇya-cakravāḍaṃ loke); ˚sthāpitāḥ (bodhisattvas); ˚sthāpayitavyaṃ (parṣanmaṇḍalaṃ).

(ppp. of pari-saṃ-sthā, of which no other form seems to be recorded except the caus., see prec., and Pali parisaṃṭhāti, in a very different mg.; ˚sthita occurs once in Crit. ed. in mg. standing round about, of attendant deities; AMg. parisaṃṭhiya, well-established,), established: (iyaṃ sarvāvatī lokadhātū …) apagatanadīmahānadī parisaṃsthitā (prose; ed. fails to separate from the prec. word). But perhaps the caus. parisaṃsthāpitā (see prec.) should be read with; no ms. is reported with it but some mss. have caus. forms, and the parallel looks in this direction.

(cf. Pali id. in mg. sets out to, tries, with dat.; see -sakkati), walks around: parisakkantaṃ (acc. sg. m. pres. pple.; but mss. ˚sakkāntaṃ or parisaṃkrāntaṃ) dṛṣṭvā, seeing him (a man covered with branches, imitating a tree) walking about.

(cf. Pkt. id.,, one of whose definitions is saṅga), sticking, cleavage: in (prose), nābhūt saṅgo vā parisaṅgoparuddhaṃgo (read ˚ddhāṅgo ?) vā upakledo vā …, said of a mahāpuruṣa, as possessor of the laksaṇa samacatvāriṃśad-danta-tā: there was no … obstructed member due to cleavage (?).
(ppp. of unrecorded pari-saṃ-tuṣ-, or cpd. of pari, intensive, and saṃtuṣṭa), completely satisfied: (prose).

(m. or nt.; see also parisāmanta, ˚taka; Pali parisamanta-to, adv., rendered from all sides, perh. lit. from the vicinity), neighborhood; only in quasi-adverbial instr. and loc., with dependent gen., near …, usually with a form of the verb carati (or a synonym): ˚ntena (nivāpasya ca ˚ntena carati); (˚ntena rājakulasya);;; ˚nte (sānaṃ); (v.l. ˚ntena). All prose.
(twice in, otherwise unrecorded), develops completely: (saṃbhavanti) parisaṃbhavanti pariniṣpadyante.
, nt., in a colophon, daśabhūmayaḥ mahāvastuparisaraṃ, acc. to introduction (from the mg. environs, vicinity); he also thinks of possibly emending to parivartam (q.v.), section.

, writhing, or stumbling? in, kāścin (women of the harem, on finding the Bodhisattva gone) nānā-kāya-parisarpikayā rudanti sma, wept with [Page332-a] various contortions, grovelings, or stumblings, of the body; Tib. rdeb, rendered by se frappent (le corps), but the meaning stumble, and others, is also given for it.
(gdve. of pari-sṛp- plus -ka), capable of being run about in (or, acc. to, easy to traverse): (sthānāni …) sukha-parisarpyakāṇi (prose; to be cultivated by an ascetic).

(AMg. id., said to be m., neighborhood; see next, and parisamanta; all seem to be variants of one word, or at least equivalents), m. noun or adj., neighboring, belonging to the vicinty: ˚ntaḥ (so Index, misprinted pārisam˚ in text; ˚samanta, but most mss. ˚sām˚) = Tib. khor yug (round about) or ñe khor (‘those about us’); in cpd., bodhimaṇḍa-˚ta-gatā(ḥ), those who were in the neighborhood of …; either adj. or acc. adv., nirdhāvati taṃ vanaṣaṇḍaṃ parisāmantaṃ (so mss., em. ˚samantaṃ), went out to that forest-thicket in the vicinity; otherwise adv. ˚te or ˚tena, with gen., = parisamanta (˚te, ˚tena): ˚te (āśramapadasya); ˚tena (kālapāśānāṃ); (āśramapadasya … carati).

(cf. sāmantaka), in Bhvr. adj. (= prec.), ardhayojana-parisāmantakaḥ, having environs (surrounding area) of half a yojana (= of that circumference?); cited by as ˚samantaka, but also ˚sām˚, no v.l.; ˚kena, adv., = ˚ntena (see prec.), (bodhimaṇḍasya).
, ppp. (recorded only in one very doubtful Vedic passage,, see), mingled, set (with precious stones): jātarūpaṃ vaiḍūrya-parisṛṣṭaṃ.
(m.; = pariṣkāra, q.v.), equipment, utensils: (no v.l.); (only v.l. parihāra); also in some citations s.v. pariṣkāra.
(unrecorded), swims thru or across: bhikṣavo 'tra (sc. arṇave, fig. of the saṃsāra) parisnānti = ˚vaḥ parisnāyanti.
(prob. caus. to Pali parippharati, suffuses, permeates), causes to expand:, so also; cite ˚sphār˚; = Tib. yoṅs su rgyas par byed pa.

, adj. (see next, and sphuṭa, pratisphuṭa; = Pali paripphuṭṭha, or ˚pphuta, read ˚ṭa ?), completely filled, full: (ābhayā);; (ratnajāla-pa˚ … gṛhaṃ);;;;;; (all these in vss, repeated);; (puṣpaphalavṛkṣaiḥ); (mahākaruṇā-pa˚); (tathāgatakāya-);;; ˚ṭaṃ tu paṭaṃ kṛtvā;;, of a magic cloth, woven and painted so as to be full (of figures).
, adj. (cf. sphūṭa, on same page of, for sphuṭa), = prec.: (prabhayā …) ˚ṭo 'bhūt (prose).

, m. or nt. (Aśokan id.), seems used in the sense of pariśraya = Pali parissaya, difficulty, trouble, perh. by folk-etym. confusion with Skt. parisrava: pratighānunayā na santi te na ca te santi mune ˚vāḥ (vs); sarvāṇi parisravāṇi ib. (vs, = pariśrayāṇi, see this).
(m., = next), filter, water-strainer: = Tib. chu tshags (˚va-kalpaḥ); a-parisrāvaṃ … pānīyaṃ, unfiltered water.

, also written ˚śrāv˚, nt. (= Pali parissāvana; cf. prec. and next), = prec.:; pātrapariśrāvaṇaṃ (dvandva, bowl and strainer) yathāsthāne sthāpya. (The preceding pātraṃ ca is to be construed with nirmādya.)
, = Pali parissā˚, ppp. of Skt. ˚srāvayati, Pali ˚ssāveti, filtered, of water:.)

, in a-pari˚, not provided with (made like) a filter or sieve, of the webbed hands and feet of a mahāpuruṣa, see s.v. jālin: vicitra-suvibhakta-chidrāparisrāviṇī (dual), (if text is right) in a manifold and well-separated way not made like a filter with holes; but perhaps read ˚chidra-pari˚, having (the nature of) a filter by reason of various well-divided holes.

, (1) (= Pali id.; cf. also parihāra, ˚hārya), once ger. ˚hārya as if from ‘caus.’ ˚hārayati, protects, guards, looks after: (śiṣya-)gaṇaṃ;; śrāvaka-, bhikṣu-saṃghaṃ;;;;;; a herd (yūtha, of deer, apes, birds, the subject being their leader), (mss. ˚reti);;;; parents (subject being their son), janetrīṃ; mātaraṃ … pitaraṃ … pariharet; pass., mātāpitarau … parihriyete; the embryo in the womb, subject the mother (so also Pali), parihārya (seemingly to *˚hārayati, but reading doubtful) kukṣiṇā; oneʼs own speech,, see s.v. parihārya; (2) (cf. umschlingen in s.v.) wraps up, a purchase (otherwise): (keśaraṃ, q.v.) parihariyāhaṃ bhagavato … adhikāraṃ karomi. pariharetsuḥ (mss.) … te duve gandhikamahattarakā śatasahasrakeśaraṃ, having wrapt up (the perfume being bought), I shall pay service to the Lord (with it). (So saying) the two perfumers wrapt up the perfume worth 100,000; (3) brings, moves (trans.; cf. umherbewegen in s.v.): bhagavāṃ dakṣiṇam eva caraṇaṃ kanakakamalaṃ, pariharati indrakīle (loc. of goal) tatra bhavati adbhuto ghoṣo (vss), in account of Dīpaṃkaraʼs entrance into Dīpavatī-city.

, nt.,, and parihāraka, nt., [in both = Tib. gdub bu, with addition of tham pa = pari in ] or ˚raka m., [˚kāḥ, n. pl., in vs]; in v.l. ˚harakaṃ, which reads without v.l.: bracelet [or anklet], acc. to Tib.; certainly some bodily ornament. The two are surely different forms of one word, which also appears in BHS as pārihāraka, q.v. It occurs in crit. ed.; and, always following a parallel form of kuṇḍala, ˚hāṭaka in text [with most mss.] but always with v.l. ˚hāraka. Taken by as noun, identical with ˚hāṭaka, but in as adj., ganz von Gold [with kuṇḍala]; the existence of the v.l. ˚hāraka, and BHS pārihāraka, give support to ʼs earlier interpretation, to which I adhere. See.)
(nt.; = Pali ˚hāna; in Skt. rare, only twice in a Brāhmaṇa, s.v., in neg. a-pari˚), loss, ruin:; abhavyaḥ ˚ṇāya (so with abhabba in Pali).
(to Skt. parihāṇi plus -kā), in pada- ˚ṇikayā, adv., ‘by diminution of a step’, one step behind (another monk): caṅkramanti ….
(nt.; to Skt. ˚hāpayati, Pali ˚hāpeti), abandonment, quitting: saṃgha-˚ṇāya.
, ppp. (= JM. ˚hāviya = Skt. Pali ˚dhāpita, to ˚dhāpayati), clothed: vastraṃ ˚to.

(m.; = Pali id.; to pariharati, 1), watchful care, guard, ward, act or process of guarding: teṣāṃ bhavanto ardhaparihārā (em.), of these (disciples) you (two) have half the guardianship (Bhvr.; are half-guardians); parihāradharmaṃ na mārgayati, he seeks not to follow the law of watchful care (of religious practices; wrongly); saparihārā śikṣā, full of watchful care (here correctly).

, adj. (quasi-gdve. to pariharati 1, or to parihāra plus -ya), guarded, of speech, opp. to saṃbhinnapralāpa: sambhinnapralāpāt prativirataḥ … suparihāryavacanaḥ [Page333-a] (Bhvr.); vacanaṃ parihāryaṃ pariharati 21, keeps his speech guarded.

, Skt., investigation, testing, of valuable things: mentions eight parīkṣā in the cliché cited s.v. udghaṭaka, q.v., etc., and ghaṭaka; single complete lists are rare but by combining the lists preceding occurrences of the cliché it seems that we get vastu-, dāru-, ratna-, hasti-, aśva-, kumāra- (or puruṣa-), kumārī (˚rikā-, or strī-), and vastra- (, in a list also containing vastu-)parīkṣā; these all occur, in different order,
= Skt. parīkṣate, examines:; cf. upaparīkṣ˚; nirīkṣyate;; Chap. 43, s.v. īkṣ (2).

, adj. (= paritta, q.v.; cf. also parīttaka, parīttaśubha, parīttābha), small, limited, restricted, minor; very common:;;;;;;;;;;;;;;; mā parīttamanām (! for ˚manas) utpādaya, donʼt be faint-hearted (‘small-minded’); a-parītta, not small,.

(nt.; = Pali 2 paritta, see, or ˚ttā), protection, safeguard, refuge (from Skt. pari-trā-): suparīttaṃ (v.l. ˚ītaṃ) bhāvayiṣyati, he (the Bodhisattva) will produce, effect, a good safeguard (refuge, against the ills of life); otherwise, but very implausibly,. The ī may be due to influence of the very common homonym, 1 parītta; but, of course, the ī of the preverb pari- is otherwise capable of lengthening in Skt.
, adj. (= Pali parittaka), = 1 parītta, q.v.: (prose); (vs, meter bad).
(= Pali parittasubha), m. pl., of limited magnificence, one (usually the 1st) of the classes of rūpāvacara gods in the 3d dhyānabhūmi; usually with deva, q.v.:;;;;; (mss. mostly parīta˚);;; etc.

(= Pali paritt˚), m. pl., of limited radiance, one (usually the 1st) of the classes of rūpāvacara gods of the 2d dhyānabhūmi; usually with deva, q.v.:;;;; and (mss. in both parītā˚);;;, etc. Once, in, seems to be used otherwise, as adj., but the expression is very strange, possibly corrupt; at the time of the Bodhisattvaʼs abhiniṣkramaṇa, the habitations of various gods became completely purified; at the end of the list, in 16, śuddhāvāsānāṃ (highest of rūpāvacara gods, and far higher than parīttābha gods) devānāṃ bhavanāni (etc.); then, in 17, evaṃ ca teṣu śuddhāvāseṣu deveṣu parīttābhānāṃ samyaksaṃbuddhānāṃ adhiṣṭhitāni caṅkramā niṣadyāni śayyāni tāni pi atīva pariśuddhāni abhūnsuḥ paryavadātā. I cannot explain the dwelling of Perfectly Enlightened Buddhas ‘of limited radiance’ among śuddhāvāsa gods.
(also pari˚; to next), the giving over, presenting: ˚nā-;; ˚nayā ( pari˚); ˚nāṃ;.
(= parin˚, q.v.), I present, hand over: ˚āmi;; ppp. ˚dita; ( parindita).

(in Skt. seems to be used in time expressions only in meaning afterwards, later, as adv., or prep. with abl. or gen., after, later than; acc. to, Pali para is used also of ‘remote past’), (1) alone, postpos. with gen., before (of remote past time; lit. beyond): kalpānāṃ p˚; (2) in collocation with following parataraṃ or ˚reṇa, as postpos. with abl. or gen., of both future and past time; future, beyond, later than, after: tataś ca bhūyaḥ pareṇa paratareṇa; (tataḥ) pareṇa paratareṇa; tataḥ pareṇa parataraṃ (prob. temporal, after that, but could possibly be local, beyond that point); [Page333-b] after gen. of noun, after, later than: pareṇa parataraṃ; (Dīpaṃkarasya) and ff.; of past time, before, long before, with prec. gen. of noun, pareṇa paratareṇa;; ˚taraṃ; in a longer phrase, prec. by abl. of pronoun or gen. of noun, tataḥ (or tebhyaḥ,, or gen. of noun,) pareṇa paratareṇa yad āsīt tena kālena (following an expression for a very long time in the past);;.
, pron. adj. (= Skt. paraspara, AMg. paroppara; not recorded in Pali), one another: ˚raṃ ca yathābhiprāyaṃ samāgacchanti.
, (1) nt. (= Pali paṇṇaka), leaf: śīrṇa-˚kāni samudānīya; feather, (paryaṅkaḥ …) tūlikāparṇakāstīrṇaḥ; (2) adj. (or parṇika = parṇin?), fem. ˚ikā, leafy, made of leaves: ˚kāṃ kuṭim abhinirmāya.

(m. or nt.), acc. to a certain kind of rice; more likely, I think, some special preparation (curry?) of rice: ekam-ekaṃ ca (sc. bhikṣuṃ) sapta-sapta puruṣā sapta-saptehi niṣṭhānehi parṇakulakena ca śālīnāṃ (so mss.; śālinā by em.!), seven men served each monk with seven dishes and with … (curry?) of rice; parṇakula-śālisya śata (mss. śaka) vāhāṃ preṣayet, sent … carts (loads) of … (? curry-)rice, i.e. of rice prepared in this style.
,, or ˚śavarī, et alibi, n. of a goddess.

, m. (= Skt. ˚ṭa, a kind of cake; AMg. pappaḍa, a thin paper-like dried cake,; in Pali only recorded in bhūmi-pappaṭaka), noted only in bhū-, bhūmi-, pṛthivī-p˚, qq.v., all of which (certainly the first two) seem clearly to mean a kind of edible mushroom (like Pali bhūmi-p˚, above); lit. earth-(pan)cake or the like.
, adj. (unrecorded), squatting in the position called (Skt.) paryaṅka: ˚naṃ et alibi; see also ardha-paryaṅkin.
, roams about: so for paryeṣatī (vs), see paryeṣati (2); so also, in the same passage,; read prob. paryaṇvate, see next.]
, roams about (cf. aṇvati): sā codyānaṃ paryaṇvantī … (vs), so by plausible em. for hopelessly corrupt and metr. deficient mss. Cf. prec.
, attains completely: sujātadarśanatvaṃ ca śreṣṭhī paryadhigacchasi (3 sg. aor.) (vs).

, (1) nt. (in Skt. only m.), end: ˚taṃ (n. sg.), prāptaṃ mayā … (at end of line of vs; in paryantaḥ … prāpto, in same series of vss; both times no v.l.); (2) at end of a cpd., pātra-paryanta, m. (= Pali patta-pariyanta,; comm. evaṃ parivattetvā pariyante ṭhitapatto), the last, worst (of its kind, here bowl), Chin. le plus laid; cf. the following; (3) adj., in obscure passage evam aparyantāḥ sarvaśākyakumārā atha paryantaś ca bodhisattvaḥ; essential mg. must be thus all the Śākya youths were unsuccessful (didnʼt get to the solution? sc. in mathematical computation), and on the other hand the B. was successful. The Tib. reads as if the two terms pary˚ and apary˚ were reversed: de ltar (= evaṃ) sā kya gzhon nu de dag (youths) thams cad (all) ni phug thug par gyur (? became arrived at end?, furent poussés à bout), byaṅ chub sems dpaḥ la ni thug paḥi mthaḥ med par gyur to (, sans que le B. eût été poussé à bout lui-même; Tib. is not quite clear to me but certainly contains a negative). If the apparent transposition in Tib. authorized the assumption that the true text was paryantāḥ śākyakumārā athāparyantaś ca bodhisattvaḥ, this and the preceding (2) would authorize setting up an adj. [Page334-a] paryanta, ‘at the end’, inferior, and then a-pa˚, not inferior. But aparyanta also occurs in its Skt. mg. of limitless; see e.g. aparyanta-tvāt, because of the limitlessness.
, adj. (to Skt. paryanta plus -ka), of the border, frontier: ˚kāḥ koṭṭarājās (vs). Cf. also next.

(or ˚taka?; Pali, see below), f. ˚tikā, ifc. (Bhvr.?), having … as its limit, ending in, limited to: kāya-˚tikāṃ vedanāṃ, and jīvita-˚tikāṃ ve˚ 4, = Pali kāya-pariyantikaṃ vedanaṃ and jīvita-par˚ (acc. sg.); these, like the forms, might be fems. to ˚taka, but in occur masc. forms (bhojana-)pariyantiko etc.

(m.; seemingly = paryāya, q.v., which perh. read ?), course, regular procedure: ifc. Bhvr. in aviparīta-paryayo (v.l. ˚pratyayā) śāstuḥ śāsane (prose), having (adopted) an unreverting course in the Teacherʼs teaching, said of one who has realized the śrotāpattiphala.

, and ppp. ˚gāḍha (= Pali pariyogāhati and ˚heti, ppp. gāḷha), examines, investigates, penetrates intellectually: ger. a-paryavagāhitvā;; ˚hetvā; (mss.); ppp. in ˚gāḍha-dharma(n) = Pali ˚ogāḷha-dhamma: ˚mā (n. sg. m.); (em.);; stem ˚ma-,, and.

, ppp. (to pary-ava-dā-, purify, recorded only in the foll. and in caus. forms chiefly with -dap- in Pali, except ˚dāta rarely in Skt.,,), completely purified: exceptionally in the sense of educated, nānāpaṇyaparīkṣāsu ˚dātaḥ sarvaśāstrajñaḥ; otherwise noted only following pariśuddha, one or the other sometimes preceded by ekānta- in comp.: ˚ddhaṃ ˚dātaṃ brahmacaryaṃ;;;;;;;; of citta,; (su-pary˚); misc.,;;.
(nt.; to prec.), complete purification: tat sarvaṃ tejasā ˚nam agacchat; sarvākuśaladharmaparyavadāna-karaṇa-tayā.
(-tva, nt.; = Pali pariyodāpaka), (state of) completely purifying: ˚tvāt.
(nt.; to next; Pali pariyodapana), complete purification: ˚nāya; sarvadharmamukha- ˚nāya.

(Pali pariyodapeti; see prec. items and next), purifies completely: ˚payati; (dharmaparyāyaṃ …) ˚payan (pres. pple.); gdve., dharmamukhāni ˚dāpayitavyāni; ppp. ˚pita,; with suffix -tā, su-paryavadāpita-tayā, because of being well purified.
(to prec.), one who purifies completely: svasya vādasya ˚tāro.

, ppp. (Skt. Gr. only; cf. next two; = Pali pariyonaddha), covered, overgrown, concealed, beset; rarely in a good sense: (bhūmipradeśaṃ), covered with useful grain; almost always in bad sense (so in Pali,); = Tib. yoṅs su dkris pa (enwrapped, esp. ensnared, as in sin); -timira-paṭalaparyava˚ (often ˚ddha-nayana, or -netra);;;;; avidyāṇḍakośapaṭala-pary˚; (˚koṣa˚); mātsaryapary˚;.
(cf. Pali pariyonandhati; Skt. regularly nahyati, also nahet, but with pary-ava-only as stated in prec.), grows over, covers: śālisya kaṇo ca tuṣo ca paryavanahe (aor.).

, m. (= Pali pariyonāha, or ˚naha = nīvaraṇa; cf. prec. items), growing over, covering [Page334-b] (only in bad senses): -timira-paṭala-paryav˚ (see paryavanaddha); in (because of the even and well-spaced teeth of the mahāpuruṣa, as he eats food: nābhūt …) paryavanāho vā (follows abhiṣyanda, q.v.; precedes abhiṣajjana or atisarjana, qq.v.), app. some pathological condition of the teeth, growing over, covering (with remnants of food ? with tartar, or decay, caries?). One might think of impacted teeth which fail to grow out, except that the whole list of non-existent defects seems modified by asyāhāraṃ paribhuñjānasya.
, m., obstruction: = Tib. yoṅs su ḥdzin pa, or ḥgag pa, bgag pa. Neither this nor any form or deriv. of pary-ava-rudh- is recorded elsewhere.

, nt. (once m.,; seems = Pali pariyuṭṭhāna in mg. 1, but see BHS paryutthāna), (1) (state of) possession (by vice or depravity; cf., where it is shown that some schools equated this with kleśa and anuśaya): nānā-dṛṣṭyanuśaya-˚na-kleśa-praśamana-kuśalaḥ (of a Bodhisattva) (= Tib. kun nas dkris pa, complete wrapping up, ensnaring); ˚nam (erroneous var. paryupasth˚) (Tib. id.), follows upakleśa; -anuśaya-parya˚, see s.v. anuśaya; kāma-chanda-˚na-duḥkhitānāṃ sattvānāṃ; a longer list of vices in cpd. ending ˚naduḥkhitānāṃ sattvānāṃ 10; -anuśayopakleśa-˚nānām; kleśa-˚nam anuśayo vā; raktānāṃ rāga-˚naṃ vigacchati; tasyā yad rāga-˚naṃ tad vigataṃ, dveṣa-˚nam utpannam, possession by passion (desire) disappeared, and possession by loathing arose; niṣparyavasthāna-jñāna-, acc. to note in = Tib. yoṅs su dkrigs pa (obscuration, instead of dkris pa, above, enwrapping), knowledge that is free from possession (by vice, impurity); (2) more particularly cpd. with krodha, possession by anger: krodha-˚na (Tib. as in above);;; ˚nena paryavasthitaḥ (Tib. as in above, for both noun and ppp.); cf. krodha-paryavasthita, under next; (3) hence, more specifically, without expression of krodha, anger (cf., with a different implication, Eng. possessed, orig. sc. by an evil spirit): tena tīvreṇa ˚nena kharavākkarma niścāritaṃ and, yadāsya ˚naṃ vigataṃ 23; tīvreṇa ca ˚nena śirasi mallakena prahāro dattaḥ; tīvreṇa ˚nena paryavasthitaḥ; tīvra-˚na-paryavasthito 'yaṃ; ˚no vigataḥ (m.!), his anger departed, tato vigata- ˚naḥ (Bhvr.) kathayati 15; ˚nam. Cf. next.

, ppp. (cf. Pali pariyuṭṭhita, but it is not clear that Pali shows the senses here recorded, corresponding to paryavasthāna 2 and 3), orig. possessed, but specifically by anger: krodha-pary˚, and see others s.v. ˚sthāna 2; alone, without krodha (see also s.v. ˚sthāna 3), or without even paryavasthāna, angry, enraged: (cf. ˚sthāna);;;;;.

(f.; n. act. to next; corresp. to Pali pariyatti = paryāpti, not used in this sense in Skt.), mastery, comprehension (of a text): (dharma-paryāyasya …) ˚āptaye (text wrongly paryāvāptaye); vācanāya paryavāptaye (cf. vācayati with paryavāpnoti).

(used like paryāpnoti, q.v., paryāpuṇati, which = Pali pariyāpuṇāti; Pali records no pariyavāp˚; cf. prec.), masters, understands (words, a speech, a text, learning): often follows parallel form of Skt. vācayati, so, vācayed vā ˚pnuyād vā; vācaya ˚pnuhi (vidyām); vācayiṣyanti ˚āpsyanti;;;; vācayitavyā … paryavāptavyā; likhiṣyanti yāvat ˚āpsyanti; ˚pnoti (dharmān); following udgṛhya (or in gṛhya), paryavāpya;;; (bhagavatā [Page335-a] bhāṣitam, what the Buddha said). The n is recorded only as dental, not domal ṇ.

(Pali pariyā˚, in ger. ˚dāya, and acc. to inf. ˚dātuṃ, also ppp. ˚dinna, and pass. ˚di(y)yati which however is also used in active mg.; see s.v. ādiyati; cf. paryādāna, a-paryātta etc.), (1) masters, overcomes; (2) exhausts. Forms: ˚dadāmi; ger. ˚dāya; inf. ˚dātum, also ˚dattum (˚datum ? see); ppp. paryātta, paryādatta, and ˚dinna; pass. ˚dīyate. Mgs.: (1) and 3 abhibhavituṃ paryāda(t)tuṃ vā, to conquer (of an army); paryādinno (gautamasya tejena), 15; ˚dātum, to overcome (a magic fluid; said of copper, meaning to turn it into copper); ˚dāya, ger.; parivartān paryādadāmi, I master (intellectually) chapters (of a text); muktvā … tathāgataṃ nānyaḥ śaktaḥ pūrṇaṃ … arthato vā vyañjanato vā paryādātum, except the Tathāgata no one else can master (overcome, surpass, in learning) Pūrṇa, either as to the spirit or as to the letter (of the texts; wrongly and); sarvaguṇavarṇa-paryādattaiḥ (ppp. but in active mg.; said of Bodhisattvas) who had mastered …; of mastering, overcoming the mind on the part of deleterious forces (cf. a-paryātta etc., with citta etc.), tac cāsya cittaṃ na paryādāya tiṣṭhati, and that does not continue mastering his mind; similarly na … cittaṃ paryādāya sthāsyati; (pāpakāḥ asadvitarkāḥ) … na (sc. cittaṃ) paryādāya tiṣṭhanti; kāmarāgo mānasaṃ paryādinnavān, love-passion mastered his mind; for see below; (2) paryādīyante (kuśalā dharmāḥ), might be understood as are overcome, repressed, but cites the passage reading parihīyante, suggesting that it means are exhausted; (pratibhāne) paryādatte, exhausted, given out, expired; paryātta-vāṣpa, whose tears are at an end.

, nt. (= Pali pariyā˚; to prec.), (1) regularly, exhaustion, giving out: esp. common in comb. parikṣayaṃ ˚dānaṃ plus a form of gacchati, give out and be completely exhausted,;;;;;;;;; na kṣīyate na ˚dānaṃ gacchati; (without parikṣaya) ˚dānaṃ (Calc. paryavadānaṃ, and so) gacchanti pātālasaṃdhigatam iva vāri;;; jīvita-paryādānād from (after) the end of life; sarvākuśaladharma-paryādāna-karaṇatayā; (2) in -viṣa-paryādāna-tayā, perhaps because of the condition of mastering (overcoming) of poison (but perhaps rather exhaustion?).

, adj. (= Pali pariyā˚; prob. pari, intensive, plus Skt. āpanna, in specialized mg., rather than ppp. of unrecorded *pari-ā-pad-), belonging to, included in, involved in: ˚naḥ = Tib. gtogs pa, belonging to; kāmadhātu-(q.v.)-pary˚;;;; trisāhasra-pary˚, belonging to the system of 3000 (great-thousand worlds); (trisāhasramahāsāhasra-)-pary˚; naika-(or other modifier)-lokadhātu-pary˚;; pūrvāntāparānta-pary˚; sarva-paryāpanna-sarva-sattva-, all beings comprised in all (classes of beings, many of which have been listed just above); tarkaparyāpannāyāṃ bhūmau sthitānāṃ; (duḥkhaṃ …) sugati-paryāpannaṃ, (misery) that is involved (even) in ‘good’ forms of existence (in addition to hell, etc., preceding); saṃgha-paryāpannaṃ śaikṣakaṃ (q.v.) karma, … ‘included in the routine of the Order’ (); pravrajyā-paryāpanno bodhisattvaḥ, … that is involved in (included in, a practitioner of) wandering monkhood; pātra-˚nnaṃ (so in Pali patta-pariyā˚), (food) that is contained in the (monkʼs) bowl.

(semi-MIndic, = paryāpnoti, q.v., and Pali pariyāpuṇāti), masters (in Pali,, rendered by jānāti; may take object dhamma): dharma (read as separate word) paryāpuṇeyā (3 sg. opt.) (text paryāyaṇeyyā) = (vs); kuśalā dharmā paryāpuṇiṣyanti (prose), will be mastered (fut. in pass. mg., representing Skt. mid.); (bhaiṣajyāṃ) paryāpunitvā (prose), having mastered (controlled) remedies; (bodhi, sā na śakyam …) paryāpunituṃ, it cannot be mastered.

(= Pali pariyattaṃ = alaṃ, it is enough), it is enough: paryāptaṃ yaṃ bhagavāṃ … eko abhiniṣkrānto, tat sādhu bhagavaṃ (mss. ˚vāṃ) rāhulakumāraṃ anujānāhi yaṃ na pravrajiṣyati (Śuddhodana to the Buddha); (Mākandikālaṃ, i.e. -ka alaṃ) paryāptam iti.

(= paryāpuṇati, q.v., but also paryavāpnoti, q.v.; in Pali only pariyāpuṇāti, or ˚ṇati, seems recorded), masters, understands (a text): ˚pnuyād, opt., (after likhāpayed); (object dharmaparyāyam; after udgṛhṇīyād and likhed, cf. paryavāp˚).

, m. (= Pali pariyāya; in these mgs. not in Skt.), (1) arrangement, disposition for doing anything: ˚yam akārṣīt … iha āgamanāya, has made arrangements to come here (so Pali, pariyāyaṃ karoti); brāhmaṇai(r) … paryāyo hy eṣa cintitaḥ, this procedure has been devised …; (2) way, means, virtually = upāya: ko nu khalv asyāt paryāyo yena …, repeated, what would be a way (means) whereby …; in this sense esp. dharma-paryāya, q.v.; cf. dharmāṇāṃ paryāya-jñānam, and paryāya alone = dharma-p˚, in (vs) tam eva 'yaṃ (so with for yaṃ) icchati bhāṣaṇāya paryāyam agraṃ tada yo mayā śrutaḥ (so with Ḱ for yaṃ … śrutaṃ); here doubtless also (vs), where mss. bodhisattvaparyāya-(unmetr., but MIndic ˚pariyāya- gives good meter and sense; em. ˚pariṣāya)-īśvarā, lords of the manner (method; of teaching, dharma-p˚) of Bodhisattvas; alternatively, ˚pariyāya = ˚yaṃ, acc. with deśayanti in 14, the Lords teach the way (manner, course, mg. 3) of bodhisattvas; (3) way, manner: loka- (so read with v.l., loke) -paryāya-kovidu, knowing the ways of the world; cetaḥ-(citta-)-paryāya, q.v., the ways of thought, of the mind (esp. of others, as known by Buddhas); anekaparyāyeṇa, in various ways, etc.; anekaparyāyeṇa asmin kāye duḥkhāni saṃkramanti; anena paryāyeṇa, in this way,;;; in this (changed, alternative) way; sometimes esp. anenāpi paryāyeṇa appears to mean even in that alternative, on that different supposition,, and prob. (parallel to); hence (4) (alternative) kind, sort, in durūpa- (q.v.; so with mss.)-paryāyā (same vs durūpam āgamya) karmā kalyāṇapāpakā ( karma ˚pakaṃ) (vs), actions are of two alternative kinds, good and bad.
, n. of the 4th division of the Yogācārabhūmi:. See saṃgrahaṇī.
(see hiṇḍati), wanders about: pres. pple. ˚ḍanto; ˚ḍantiye (gen. sg. f.).

, nt. (= Pali pariyuṭṭhāna; used substantially like paryavasthāna, in mg. 1, q.v.; cf. note on, ‘la distinction entre paryavasthāna et paryutthāna paraît surtout verbale; il y a paryut˚ lorsque la passion se lève … paryava˚ lorsque la passion enveloppe’; so Tib. kun nas ldaṅ ba, rising all around, for paryut˚), rising all about, overwhelming, possession (always by depravities or vices): sarvāvaraṇa-vivaraṇaparyutthāna-vigataḥ; ˚nam (after anuśaya, before upakleśa and paryavasthāna); ˚na-viṣkambhaṇamātreṇa [Page336-a] (with merely blocking the uprising, sc. of depravities) tuṣṭiṃ vindati, na cānuśayasamudghātāya (see) mārgaṃ bhāvayati; ˚na-viṣkambhanam; kaukṛtyapary˚; (after akaukṛtyatā) aparyutthānatā, state of having no possession (by depravities); nivaraṇāvaraṇa-pary˚; niṣpary˚ (= a-pary˚, above); vigatarāga-doṣa-moha-paryutthānāṃ; paryutthāna-kiśalayā nirdagdhā jñānatejena (referring to anuśaya in prec. line) (vs), the ‘shoots’ (fig., alluding to literal mg. of paryutthāna) of the risings-up of (possession by) them (the anuśaya) have been burnt out by the fire of knowledge.
, erroneous var. for paryutthāna; and for paryavasthāna.]

, nt., and ˚nā (= AMg. pajjuvāsaṇa; Skt. in nearly the same mg.; to Skt. paryupāste in similar sense; Pali payirupāsana, ˚nā, ˚sati), respectful, reverent waiting upon, service, worship: ˚nam; vandanāya ˚nāya ca (of the Bodhisattva); ˚nāya (of Buddha); (read with mss. upasaṃkramaṇaṃ ˚nāya, for purposes of worship, of Buddhas); ˚nāya (of Buddha) also;; (bhagavantaṃ darśanāyopasaṃkramitūṃ ˚nāya); (vandanāya ˚nāya; so also;); ˚nena (misprinted paryupas˚); ˚sana˚ in comp. (here could be ˚sanā˚); (in both these of kalyāṇamitrāṇi); f., bhagavantaṃ darśanāyopasaṃkramiṣyāmi ˚nāyai;.

, ppp. of Skt. paryupāste (cf. prec.; normally in passive sense, honored, revered, respectfully attended, e.g.;, cited from; but also) in active sense, having honored, revered, attended: ˚tāḥ sugata (object); na … te … ekabuddha-paryupāsitā bhaviṣyanti, they will not have served one Buddha (only); bahubuddhaśatasahasraparyupāsitair (Bodhisattvas); bahubuddhaparyupāsitaḥ (Mañjuśrī).

() = prec., in active sense: bahubuddhakoṭīnayutaśatasahasra-˚tāvino (… tathāgatāḥ); similarly (buddha …) ˚tāvinas te … bhaviṣyanti, they shall become ones-who-have-worshiped … Buddhas, i.e. shall accomplish such worship.

(Skt., ppp. of pari-vas), in ˚ta-parivāsa (see also 1 parivāsita; = Pali parivuttha-(or ˚ṭṭha-)parivāsa, in technical sense, see parivāsa), (1) having undergone probation:;; ˚ta-mūlaparivāsaḥ, and mūlāpakarṣa-paryuṣito ib. (see mūla 3); mūlaparivāsa-paryuṣitaḥ; (2) having completed residence (in heaven; said of gods reborn there after having been lower beings previously; is divine existence regarded as a kind of probation? prob. merely change of residence, sc. from earth): in a cliché;, nāsmākaṃ pratirūpaṃ syād yad vayaṃ paryuṣitaparivāsā bhagavantaṃ darśanāyopasaṃkrāmema, yan nu vayam aparyuṣitaparivāsā eva …, it would not be proper that we should approach the Blessed One to see him after finishing our residence (probation?); let us, while this is still unfinished, (visit him); similarly.
(for Pali and BHS 2 parivāsita; form app. assimilated, by some analogical process, to 1 paryuṣita = Skt. id.), perfumed: candana-karpūrakuṅkuma- ˚ṣitena; -paryuṣite.

(m.? cf. paryeṣati 2, with its ppp. paryeṣita), circumference, enclosure, circle, orig. seemingly a going around: in Bhvr. cpds., samanta-jvālāvabaddha- (text ˚buddha)-maṇḍala-paryeṣaḥ (of a figure of Mañjuśrī), lit. having a round-about-flame-bound-circle-circumference (or enclosure); ratnaprabhāvicchurita-dyoti-paryeṣam (acc. sg.; of a Tathāgata) [Page336-b], having a jewel-radiance-covered-light-circumference (or enclosure);, auréolé du rayonnement fulgurant des joyaux (similarly 31 for passage above, entouré …).
, adj. or subst. m. (to paryeṣati with aka), seeking, one who seeks: asadguṇa-paryeṣakasya; yathābhilāṣiṇo yathāvastuparyeṣakān.
(Skt. Gr. id., = Pali pariyesanā; Skt. ˚ṇa, nt.), seeking, striving after: ˚ṇāṃ; (pakṣa-; here ed. em. ˚ṇaṃ); ˚ṇā (bhogānāṃ);;;.

, rarely (semi-MIndic). pariyeṣate (Skt. ˚ṣati, rare, cited once from; Pali pariyesati; only in mg. 1; cf. prec. and following items), (1) seeks, searches for, strives after: ˚ṣanti (bodhisattvacaritaṃ); (vs; object tīrthe, acc. to religious teachers); ˚ṣate. (bhakta); (kanyāṃ);;; (śastraṃ; last four prose); ˚ṣase; ˚ṣante (kāyaśuddhiṃ); impv. ˚ṣatha;; ˚ṣadhvam; pple. ˚ṣamāṇa;;;; (=); m.c. pariyeṣamāṇaḥ (vs); and even in prose, parato vā pariyeṣitaiḥ (sc. bhogaiḥ), or with such as have been sought from others; paryeṣyanti (vs, only one ms., but that the best, has y after ṣ); paryeṣyāmaḥ (prose, but v.l. ˚ṣāmaḥ); ˚ṣayanto, pres. pple.,; fut. ˚ṣayiṣyāmi; ger. ˚ṣayitvā; ppp. paryeṣita-(Tib. yoṅs su btsal ba, thoroughly sought)-sarvakuśalamūlasya; a-paryeṣitam, unsought, after a-mārgitam,, and doubtless read so in close parallel (both prose) with for a-paryeṣṭam (with only 2 Nep. mss.!) in both edd. (cf. however paryeṣṭi, which supports paryeṣṭa as a possibility); (2) wanders around: parinirvṛto pī (so read with v.l. and, m.c.) imu sarvalokaṃ paryeṣatī (paryaṇṭhate) sarvadaśaddiśāsu (vs), tho entered into nirvāṇa, He wanders over (so Tib., yoṅs su rgyu) this whole world …; hence, ppp. paryeṣita, gone around, enclosed, encompassed: samanta-jvālā-māla-(= mālā, perh. read so)-paryeṣitāṃ (prose; of a figure of Tārā), enclosed by a garland of flames on all sides; so,; see paryeṣa.

, f. (= Pali pariyeṭṭhi; to paryeṣati), search, striving for, seeking; often with worldly things as the object, āhāra-cāvara-paryeṣṭi-hetoḥ;;, seeking for food and raiment; apariśuddhajñānakṣānti-saṃbhoga-paryeṣṭiḥ (… duḥkhavipāko dharmaḥ); lābha-paryeṣṭy-arthaṃ; lokāyatamantra-paryeṣṭi-tā; or with implication but no expression of such objects, paryeṣṭi-vyasanādīni duḥkhāni; ˚ṭi-samudācāra-duḥkhaṃ; ˚ṭiduḥkhānugatāṃ … gṛhasthatāṃ; ˚ṭi-nidānaṃ (see nidāna 1); but also with expressed or implied neutral, or even religiously commendable, objects (as in Pali pariyeṭṭhi), mantracaryāparyeṣṭiḥ; śruta-p˚; buddhadharma-p˚;; dharma-p˚; ˚ṭim (for religious enlightenment) āpadyeyaṃ (or ˚haṃ), to be restored also in (cf. and parallel paryeṣamāṇaḥ).

, (1) prob. error (but see s.v. parvan!) for parva(n), joint of a plant: -gaṇḍa-parvatapattra-palāśa-puṣpa-; (2) n. of a former Buddha: (cf. Parvataś(i)rī); (3) n. of a yakṣa:. (Also n. of the well-known brahmanical sage, associate of Nārada:.)

, nt., also parva, nt. and m. (in mss. sometimes written parvata, which is prob. a mere corruption; cf. s.v. parvata 1, where the same is recorded for parva(n) in mg. joint of a plant; in mg. holiday = AMg. pavva, nt.; cf. Skt. parvan, day of change of the moonʼs phases, which was a holiday; hence this more generalized mg.), holiday: kim idaṃ … parvaṃ (v.l. parva) vā prayogaṃ vā utsavaṃ vā; (kiṃ) atra nagare parvo 'yaṃ, is today a holiday in this town? and 16 (na adya) kiṃcit parvo na utsavo; parvaṃ (v.l. parvataṃ), see Giriyagra-samāja; nagara-parva pratyupasthitam; sālabhañjikā nāma parvataṃ (so mss., one perhaps parvanaṃ, dental n; em. parva; read parvaṇaṃ, n. sg.? so in next) pratyupasthitam; parva (mss. parvata[ṃ]), see Girivalgu-samāgama; kasmiṃścit parvaṇy upasthite; parva pratyupasthitam; parva (mss. parvaḥ!) pratyupasthitam.
(= Skt. parṣad plus -ka, Bhvr.), assembly, ifc. Bhvr.: jita-p˚; sa-p˚.
(= pariṣ˚, Skt. parṣad;), assembly: ˚dānāṃ (prose); ˚dāyāṃ (vs), so em. m.c., for pariṣ˚, some mss., or v.l. parṣadi with different following text but correct meter.
, m. (= pāriṣ˚, pārṣ˚, pariṣ˚), member of an assembly: amātya-p˚ (vs), but same cpd. with pārṣ˚ (vs).
(for parṣā plus vant; short a can hardly be called m.c. since ā would also be possible metrically), attended by an assembly, or by the (four) assemblies (of a Buddha): parṣavantāna tāyinām (vs).
(= pariṣā, etc.; Skt. parṣad), assembly: (vs); (prose); of the four assemblies of a Buddha (see s.v. pariṣā),; (both vss); (prose).
, m. (etym. not clear), app. point (of a spear), see kunta-p˚.
, m. (= Pali and Skt. Lex. id.), mason, plasterer:;;;.
, pple. (to Skt. palāyati; = Pali id., cf. next, and), fled: in prob. read palāt' (for text palātv) asurendrāḥ, the asura-lords fled ().

, pple. (= JM. palāṇa,, cf. prec., and), fled, or sometimes seemingly with pass. force, put to flight, with instr. of person causing the flight, e.g. bhagavatā te (mss. tena) amanuṣyakā (demons) palānā; so several times, regularly with instr.; used absolutely, without instr., fled,;;. Cf. also palāyaka, with v.l. palānaka, and prapalāna.
, m., a fugitive: (vs), but palāyitaḥ, and with Ḱ palānakaḥ = palānaḥ, see palāna and.
(m. or nt.; once in) or palāpa (= Pali id.; so of. both times), chaff: niṣpal˚; (both edd. with Nep. mss. ˚va), free from chaff.

(m. or nt.), ˚cikā (to pali = pari plus a form of Skt. kuc-, kuñc-, bend, cf. Skt. saṃkuc-, bring together, close; AMg. paliuñcai, in diff. mg., conceals a fault, deceives), (thatched) hut, in most cases prec. by kaṭa-, of grass, straw: kaṭa-palikuñcikāyām, text, loc sg.,;; (all prose), but mss. vary greatly one v.l. each time palikuñce; niveśanasyo (so Nep. mss., m.c. for ˚sya) palikuñcikesmin (read as one word, loc. of [Page337-b] ˚ka) (vs; has very different and certainly secondary reading; here ˚syopari ku˚; this division is inconsistent with the above forms where kaṭa- precedes pali˚; in these read kaṭapali-kuñc˚, with printed hyphen! which I cannot interpret at all): Tib. khyim gyi druṅ du rtsva yi spyil po na, in a hut of straw, or grass, near the house.
