, adj., and ˚kā, subst. (for alternative Pali and BHS forms see below), causing fall (to an evil existence, if not repented and expiated); this is clearly the usual Northern interpretation; one of the three main kinds of monkish transgressions, the others being pārājika and saṃghāvaśeṣa, qq.v.: as adj., ˚ka with dharma, (trayāṇāṃ dharmāṇām anyatamānyatamena dharmeṇa vadet pārājikena vā saṃghāvaśeṣeṇa vā) pātayantikena vā; there are 30 offenses called niḥsargikāḥ (q.v.) pātayantikā dharmāḥ, listed in the following where each is called ˚gikā ˚yantikā (subst. fem.),; they are followed by 90 pātayantikā dharmāḥ, each again styled pātayantikā (subst. fem.); ˚tikā dharmāḥ also = Tib. ltuṅ byed, lit. making fall, usually rendered transgression; the Pali correspondents are 30 nissaggiyā pācittiyā dhammā, each one styled nissaggiyaṃ pācittiyaṃ (nt., not f.) id. 18, etc., followed by 92 pācittiyā dhammā,, each one styled pācittiyaṃ On the various forms of Pali and BHS see (besides older treatments, now obsolete),, and esp.., who says inter alia: ‘In den späteren Turfanfragmenten erscheint ganz allgemein als Sanskritform pātayantikā’ (so e.g. op. cit.). He notes that pāteti is used in Pali in explaining pācittiya,, and that pātayati is similarly used in BHS in explaining the mg. of other (substitute) forms, see below. He states that Chin., like Tib. (regularly ltuṅ byed, above), supports this mg. On the other hand he reports a BHS ms. reading pāca(tt)i, which reminds one of the Pali form; and shows that pātayantika, and other alternative forms, are rendered in ways which suggest association (certainly unhistorical) with root pac-; he cites a passage () reading pātayantikā, pacati dahati uddahati avyutthitasyāvaraṇakṛtyaṃ karoti, tenāha pātayantikā, and compares pāyantiketi (text pāpānti˚, as also; in mss. pāyantikām, read thus all three times with l. c. above) dahati pacati pātayati (so with for text yāt˚). Besides the popular etymology pāpāntikā of the mss., just cited, gives pāpātmikā for Tib. ltuṅ byed. The same word is read pāyattikāḥ (sc. dharmāḥ) [Page340-b]; (naiḥsargikāḥ, q.v., = niḥsa˚) pāyattikāḥ, and pāpattikā (f.), but with vv.ll. in one or more of these places (besides pāyattikā in the last) pāyantika (pāyantikām āpattim, acc.,), pāpantika, pāṭāyantika, pātavantika, (acc. to also pādayantika,) and with ˚kā as subst. f. (pāyantikayā, instr.,). There is moreover (besides pācatti cited by above) prāyaścittikāḥ (sc. dharmāḥ) (śuddha-p˚, acc. to Tib. only, merely prāy˚, ḥbaḥ zhig tu ḥgyur ba); (snāna-)prāyaścittikaṃ (both these = Tib. ltuṅ byed); and prāyaścittikaḥ (sc. dharmaḥ) (= Tib. ltuṅ ba, fall), which is followed by śuddha- (Tib. ma ḥdres pa, unmixed) -pāpattikaḥ (sc. dharmaḥ; Tib. again ltuṅ ba, = prec.), cf. above, and s.v. śuddhaka. l. c. points out the phonetic difficulty of deriving Pali pācittiya from BHS prāyaścittika, and proposes an orig. *prākcitta plus -ika, thru *paccittika to pāci˚, la pensée en avant, = either (des actes commis) avec précipitation, or qui précipitent (aux enfers). He cites a Tocharian loan pāyti, which he says goes back to pāyantika. It is obvious that the orig. form and mg. of the word can not be confidently reconstructed.

(= Pali purisa-damma-sā˚; expl. essentially as here interpreted), charioteer (driver, tamer, controller) of human ones-that-need-to-be-tamed (= trained religiously; as indicates, dam = vi-nī, discipline); the figure clearly refers to taming animals, particularly horses, and indeed is no doubt directly based on Pali assa-damma-sārathi, q.v. in; cf. such expressions as puruṣājāneya (see s.v. ājāneya), noble steed of a man. (on, etc.) skyes bu ḥdul baḥi (of human [to-be-] tamed ones, more lit. of [to-be-] tamed men) kha lo (b)sgyur ba (helm-governor = charioteer). In Tocharian yātäṣlyes yāpy ā(śa)nt, leader of one to be tamed (omitting puruṣa; yāpy is uncertain, possibly helm as in Tib.). Regularly in cliché listing characteristics of a Buddha:;;;;;;;;;;;; etc.; etc.;; in (read with mss., and print the sentence as an āryā vs, not prose as in) puruṣasiṃhasārathinā (em. puruṣadamya˚), controller of lions of men, evidently meant as a much stronger variant of the usual term, but incidentally confirms our interpretation of the latter; so also does the epithet puruṣadamyasārathinā in another formulaic series of epithets applied to the Bodhisattva just before his enlightenment, in which several preceding epithets compare him to animals, such as puruṣarṣabheṇa, puruṣasiṃhena:;;;;; in less formulaic passages; abstr. ˚sārathi-tā, state of being …, meaning the state of Buddhahood which Bodhisattvas are to attain:;.

in (vs) puṣpaiḥ (so all mss., em. puṣpa-, kept by without note) prakāraiḥ samalaṃkṛtaṃ ca; acc. to Tib. adorned with many flowers (me tog maṅ pos). On the face of the reading of the mss. and the Tib. rendering, prakāra should be an adj., many; it is otherwise known only as a noun, kind, sort. ʼs em. hardly helps; with kinds of flowers could not, so far as I know, serve as a substitute for with many kinds …; for this we should expect bahu-, nānā-, or the like, modifying prakāra. I have thought of reading pravāraiḥ, taking it as = pravaraiḥ, excellent, with ā for a m.c.; but Tib. does not support this.

request?) is; (4) désignation acc. to, where ˚ti-dharma is contrasted with dravya-dharma, chose en soi; notation, (Tib. brtags, signe, symbole; Chin. kia, faux, simulé); ‘le mot désigne la notion comme purement verbale, comme moyen de se faire entendre’; lokānuvartanāṃ buddhā anuvartanti laukikīṃ, prajñaptim anuvartanti yathā lokottarām api (vss), … Buddhas imitate (or follow) the conventions (which pass current in the world; i.e. they seem to carry on worldly activities) as if (all this were) super-worldly (esoterically real); bahubhir abhilāpaiḥ prajñaptaya upacārāḥ (access) kriyante, and repeatedly in sequel, esp. in cpd. ˚ti-vāda; (rūpādisaṃjñake) vastuni yā rūpam ity evam-ādyāḥ prajñaptayaḥ tāḥ saṃvṛtaya (see saṃvṛti) ity ucyante; nāma-saṃketa-˚tiḥ; (nāmadheyamātraṃ saṃketamātraṃ saṃvṛtimātraṃ) prajñaptimātraṃ (said of the 5 saṃskāra; note samvṛti again, virtually = prajñapti); wrong actions are of two sorts, some like adultery wrong by nature (prakṛti-duṣṭa-tvād), others like remaining in the householderʼs life blameworthy by convention (prajñapti-sāvadya-tvād); Buddhas are prajñapti-samatikrāntā(ḥ), passed beyond convention (exoteric things); in (vs) an ātman exists prajñapti-satyato, by (exoteric) verbal convention, it is not dravya-sat, real in itself (cf., above), and so in line 11, skandhānāṃ skandhatā tadvat prajñaptyā na tu dravyataḥ, … by conventional designation, not in reality; (5) arrangement, provision (of a seat; n. act. to prajñapayati 2, prajñapta 1): śatasāhasrikā āsana-prajñaptī kriyati, a seat-provision worth 100,000 was made, i.e. a seat worth that was provided; similarly, āsanaprajñaptī ca me na tādṛśī bhaviṣyati.

(= Pali paṇidahati, paṇidheti,), orig. fixes firmly the mind (cittam, manas), but often with ellipsis of such an object, used absolutely, makes an earnest wish, cherishes an ardent desire (praṇidhāna, praṇidhi, qq.v.) for something (usually dat., sometimes loc., rarely acc.), vows, assumes a vow; sometimes (like the related nouns; and cf. apraṇihita) applied to worldly desires, so praṇidadhāti, used absolutely, synonym of abhidhyām utpādayati, and lobhacittam utpādayati, in the context; usually some sort of religious purpose is involved, so: praṇidhehi tuvaṃ tatra śreṣṭhikule cittaṃ upapattīye (prob. loc., cf. kule in 14 below), concentrate your mind on being born there in a merchantʼs family (with the understanding that he should become a monk), and cf. śreṣṭhisya kule [Page360-a] cittaṃ praṇihitaṃ 14; the wish may be for the enlightenment (bodhi, or the like) of others: evaṃ ca (sc. Sujātā) praṇidadhāti sma (‘after eating my food, may the Bodhisattva attain enlightenment!’); bodhāya cittam atulaṃ praṇidhāya sattvāṃ (gen. pl.) (vs), fixing our minds in an unequalled degree on the enlightenment of creatures (Bodhisattvas speaking); varāgrasattve praṇidhenti bodhaye (vs), (women) earnestly wished for enlightenment for (loc., lit. in the case of) the Supreme Being (the Bodhisattva); but commonly the object is enlightenment or Buddhahood for the maker of the vow, which is very often taken under the inspiration of an earlier Buddha: (bodhāya cittaṃ) praṇidadhad, fixing the mind on enlightenment; bodhāye (or ˚ya) praṇidhento, pres. pple., (mss. often praṇidhyanto); ˚dheti (narasiṃhatāye, for Buddhahood); ˚dhesi (aor.; used absolutely) = =;; purā praṇidhitvā (ger.; absolute); ˚dhenti (bodhāye); mss. ˚dhenti, ˚dhyanti, em. ˚dhento (bodhāya); ˚dhintāna (gen. pl. pres. pple.; ˚dhentāna) bodhāya (vs); ˚dhenti (samyaksaṃbodhāye); (buddhatvāya); ˚dhento (bodhāya); yebhir manaḥ praṇihitaṃ varabuddhabodhau (vs); yaṃ mayā bodhāya praṇihitaṃ that (or, since) I have made a vow for enlightenment; bodhāye praṇihitaṃ; with cognate noun, asaṃkhyeya-praṇihitā praṇidhi (sc. for bodhi); with goal in acc., praṇidhisi (m.c. for ˚dhesi, 2 sg.) cārīkām asamām (vs), thou vowest the matchless course (of a Bodhisattva), and similarly praṇidhisi (samantabhadrām … cārika, acc.).

, nt. (m. modifiers; = Pali paṇidhāna; like praṇidhi, n. act. to praṇidadhāti, praṇidheti), fixation of mind (ceto-pra˚;; Pali ceto-paṇidhi), and so ardent desire, earnest wish, vow; sometimes (but rarely) of purely worldly desires, which are reprobated, praṇidhāna-vivarjitam (vs); usually religious at least in basis, fulfilment being expected on the ground of acts of merit, which are often mentioned in a solemn declaration of wish; the thing desired may nevertheless be worldly (wealth, or special marks of grace), tho often the intention is stated to use it for religious-purposes: (magic possession of garlands); (fortunate rebirths);; (to become a cakravartin); or it may be truly religious, yet not Buddhahood or Bodhisattvahood, (here made by a past Buddha, to do services to Buddhas to come); most commonly to win enlightenment, i.e. to become a Buddha,; (˚na-paripūryai, so with mss.; cf. praṇidhi-paripūriye);;;;;;;;;; praṇidhāna-caryā, a whole course of praṇidhānas,, see s.v. caryā; when made by a Bodhisattva it may mean rather the vow to follow the Bodhisattva-course, and may then be called specifically caryā-pra˚, or bhadracarī-pra˚, etc.; praṇidhāna is one of the ten bala of a Bodhisattva,, and one of his vaśitā,; anuloma-pra˚, continued successive pra˚, seems to mean a pra˚ repeated by the same individual (Śākyamuni in previous incarnations as cakravartin), in similar terms, as described later in; there are ten mahāpraṇidhāna of a Bodhisattva,, described at length (ten such are referred to in, but the list quoted from another source by, is quite different from the list); four pūrva-praṇidhāna-padāni, each described in the sequel in an entire paragraph; three kinds of pra˚, viz. susthāna-prābandhikam (see prābandhika), sattvārtha-prābandhikam, buddhakṣetra-pariśodhakam. Rarely prārthanā, q.v., appears to be used of the ‘earnest wish’ for enlightenment.

, m., sometimes f., even nt. (= Pali, and once BHS, paṇidhi, q.v., f. acc. to, m. acc. to; both are right) = praṇidhāna, q.v. for development of mgs.; gender f., (praṇidhiṃ …) yā ti (= te) abhūṣi (vs); yā praṇidhi (vs); saiṣā te … praṇidhī (vs); ˚dhī … paripūrṇā (vs); ˚dhī iyam evarūpā (mss. ˚pāḥ) (vs); prathamā praṇidhi (v.l. ˚mo ˚dhiḥ); caturthī tadā praṇidhiḥ āsīt; pañcamā ˚dhiḥ; prathamā ˚dhir (these in all prose); neut., taṃ yuṣmākaṃ mūlapraṇidhiṃ (complete sentence!); dvitīyapraṇidhiṃ tadāsi, then was the 2d pra˚ (em. ˚yo praṇidhi); of worldly desires, nāstīha me praṇidhi saṃskṛtasarvakāmaiḥ (vs), and so in a-praṇidhi, q.v.; religious in basis, for desired fate in rebirths on basis of past merit,; of religious desires, but other than Buddhahood or Bodhisattvahood,; (Trapuṣa and Bhallika had made a praṇidhi in a former birth that the Buddha might ‘turn the wheel of the law’ after eating their food; this was fulfilled); a Bodhisattva is called praṇidhī-sāgaru, an ocean of pious vows; mūlapra˚, the original or primary vow leading to ultimate enlightenment,; commonly of the vow to gain enlightenment,;;;;;;; praṇidhi-paripūriye (so mss., instr., see s.v. praṇidhāna-paripūryai); paripūritavya praṇidhī (vs); to this, the common, sense also belong the citations of pra˚ with f. and nt. gender, above.

(if correct, cpd. of Skt. dhyāyati), meditates on: ˚dhyenti te prathamajanmasthitāḥ (vs); object may be in prec. line 23, sarvaṃ jināna aparāntaviyūhameghān, but this could be object of paśyanti in line 22, in which case ˚dhyenti could be an error for ˚dhenti, make a solemn vow, to praṇidheti, ˚dadhāti, q.v. for similar corruptions recorded in mss. of.

, adj. (= Pali paṇīta, esp. of food, but also of dhamma, sattā, creatures, etc.), superior, excellent, distinguished, first-class; esp. of food (and drink) and sometimes used, without noun, of fine food: ˚ta-vijñāpanam, asking for fine food, = Tib. zas (food) bsod pa (good) sloṅ ba (begging), something forbidden to monks by (˚ta-bhojanāni …); elsewhere, of food (sometimes drink),;; =;;;, etc.;;, etc. (common);;;, etc. (common); (rasāṃ praṇītāṃ, acc. pl.); of living creatures (sattva), esp. bracketed with hīna, low, sometimes also with madhya(ma), middling,;;;;;;; of dharma,; (opp. hīna);;; of divine existences, (devanikāya); and (trayastriṃśa); misc., (unspecified; = Tib. gya nom pa); (see prajñapta); (jñānaṃ); (praṇīta-mukhamaṇḍalaḥ, having an excellent round mouth, or face); (dhyānasukhaṃ); (dāna); (bodhimārga); (kāma, desires = desirable things); and (ratanaṃ); (artha, the goal of the Bodhisattva); (vastu).
(MIndic extension in -a of Skt. praṇetar), leader, guide: vinā praṇetareṇa (v.l. ˚tāreṇa) (prose).
, adj. (ppp. of Skt. pra-tanoti; in this mg. seems not recorded), extensive, great: paritrāyate tasmād vicitrāt pratatād ugrād bhayāt; (kusīdo nodagra-)pratata-vīrya-samanvāgataḥ.
(m. or nt.), perhaps = Pali patara (; [Page361-a]; = Skt. pradara,), hole, crevice: pratarādiṣu mahārogaspṛṣṭāsu (! but the interpretation is far from certain).
, adj. (gdve. to pra-tark-; cf., a-pra˚), discoverable: mā jñātīnāṃ ˚kyo bhaviṣyati.
(Skt., creeper, tendril), lit. creeper, tendril, used fig. of lightning, cf. the common vidyul-latā: vidyutpratāna-jvalitaṃ (so with all mss. but one for ˚taḥ).
, m., (1) n. of a large number of former Buddhas:; (2) = next, prob. only by corruption: (no v.l.); some mss. read so in (vs), but unmetrically.

, m., n. of a hot hell:, so with v.l., Tib. rab tu tsha ba, and without v.l., for text mahātāpanaḥ;; in these and most other places occurs in lists of various hells (cf. Pratāpa 2);;;;;;;;;, etc.;; (text pretāyane!); (text pretāpane! some copyist thought of preta);.
, n. of two former Buddhas: (˚ntaṃ, acc., ˚ntas, nom.); ˚vān, n. sg.
, adv., read with v.l. ˚ṭhakayā, or with ˚ṭhikayā (= Skt. pratikaṇṭham), singly, severally, one by one:.

(nt.; n. act. to Skt. pratikaroti), expiation; in yathādharma-˚ṇa-tā, state or condition of making expiation according to what is right: vyatikrāntena ca ˚ṇatayā pratyāpattiḥ karaṇīyā; (skhalitasya) ca ˚ṇatāyai vīryam.

, (1) (= Pali paṭi˚,) imitates (with dat. of person): ko nāma śaktaḥ pratikartu tubhyam (vs); naiva kadācit pratikartu śakyam 11 (vs); (2) works in accordance with what is expected, acts normally: kaccid dhātavaḥ pratikurvanti, see s.v. yāpanīya (, sont-ils en parfaite harmonie?).

(nt.), ˚ṇā (unrecorded; cf. next items), (1) desire: akāla-˚ṇa-tā mārakarma, state of having untimely desires; (2) expectation: vipāka- ˚ṇā-viśuddhaṃ (dānaṃ), free of expectation of reward; (dānaṃ) vipākāpratikāṅkṣaṇa-tā (˚ka-aprati˚); sarvadāneṣu vipākāpratikāṅkṣaṇa-cittaṃ.

(in Skt., and Pali paṭikaṅkhati, seems recorded only in mg. desires, longs for; cf. however Pali bhaya-paṭikaṅkhin, expecting dangers), waits for, expects; noted only in ppp. ˚kṣita, once, and otherwise gdve. ˚kṣitavya; na paraḥ ˚kṣitavyaḥ, I must not wait for another (to do my duty as a Bodhisattva); bhikṣubhyaḥ sakāśād ānanda mātṛgrāmeṇa pravrajyopasaṃpad bhikṣuṇībhāvaḥ ˚kṣitavyaḥ; ˚kṣitavyaḥ (context suggests to be expected); ˚tavya, various forms, (vṛddhi); (id.); (trīṇi bhayāni); (śrotrarogo na …); (vipākaḥ); (puṇyakriyāvipākaḥ); ˚kṣitaḥ, ppp., (a return for a favor done, not expected).
(cf. prec.), expectation, hope: read ˚āṃ with Corr. for text pratijñāṃ (meter demands the correction); see s.v. uttārayati. Cf. also a-pratikāṅkṣa-tā.
, adj. (denom. ppp.; = Pali paṭikujjita), covered, enclosed:, one Tib. version is bskor ba, surrounded; ayaḥprākāraparikṣiptā ayasā pratikubjitāḥ (of hell-inhabitants); ayasā prati˚ (of the same).

, nt., would seem to be a part of a city gate: (teṣāṃ dvārāṇāṃ dvinnāṃ) varṇānāṃ pratikūlaṃ [Page361-b] abhūṣi, suvarṇasya ca rūpyasya ca. The parallel passage seems, as far as I see, to have no correspondent, unless far-reaching corruption has concealed relationship. Could this be for *prati-kūṭa, as if counter-pinnacle?

, in kṛta-prati˚, adj. (to Skt. pratikṛti, app. not recorded in this sense of requital, repayment, but Skt. pratikaroti and Pali paṭikara are so used), one of the six upāya of a Bodhisattva, containing, consisting of or concerning requital (repayment) for (favors previously) done (by the Bodhisattva; he declines any recompense, other than virtuous life by his debtor):; described

, ger. used as adv. (= Pali paṭigacca, with Pkt. g for k,; usually followed by eva, i.e. ˚gacc' eva), in advance, always foll. by eva: mss. sometimes pratikṛtyaivaṃ (so); in;;;; prakṛ˚ for pratikṛ˚; and mss. often ˚tyeva (or ˚tveva; ˚tyevaṃ) for ˚tyaiva; reads always prakṛtyaiva, rendering simplement, sans aucun appareil qui fasse connaître ton rang (), tho his mss. read pratikṛ˚ in;; and; moreover the mg. he assumes for his reading prakṛtyaiva can hardly be correct, since in and the word is preceded by prākṛtakena veṣeṇa, in common garb, which would be duplicated by the assumed prakṛtyaiva: pratikṛtyaiva (text with mss. ˚vaṃ) dharmavihāry …, even in advance (of enlightenment, while still dwelling in worldly life, in the harem), he (the Bodhisattva) was dwelling according to what was right;;;;;;;;.

, ppp., adj. (= Skt. Lex. id., Pali paṭikiṭṭha; see s.v. pratikruṣṭa, where it is suggested that both Pali forms may derive from pratikṛṣṭa historically, ˚kruṣṭa being hyper-Skt.; but possibly the two are independent, tho virtual synonyms): bad, evil: ayaṃ bodhisattvasya pratikṛṣṭo mṛṣāvāda iti.

(= Pali paṭikopayati, breaks, violates. uposathaṃ; in Skt. only the noun pratikopa is recorded, from a spurious vs of,), attacks, or rebels against: ˚yanti (prajñāpāramitāṃ; parallel with pratikrośanti).

, abstains (from sin, abl.): mss. in (vs) paruṣavacanāc ca naravara pratikramāmi tathaivaṃ paiśunyaṃ (read ˚yāt, or with ˚yā, abl.); em. to prativiramāmi, which to be sure seems to be intended by prativiremi of mss. in parallel; but there is no need to em.; the ppp. pratikrāntaḥ is evidently meant in a closely similar way in, in a list of ‘synonyms for nisṛjā’, abstained, withdrawn (from evil).
, (1) nt., recession; only in association with abhikrānta 3, q.v.; (2) ppp. as adj., see pratikramati.

, adj. (felt as ppp. of Skt. prati-kruś- which is not used in an appropriate mg.; = Pali paṭikuṭṭha, which is a synonym of paṭikiṭṭha and may represent historically another form of pratikṛṣṭa, q.v.; to this our word may be a hyper-Sktism;; yet cf. next): poor, bad, inferior: of land,; ˚ṭam etad vairāṇāṃ yad uta strīvairam; similarly; compv. ˚ṭa-tara, of an occupation, low, despicable: pratikruṣṭataraṃ bāṇijyānāṃ yad uta kāṣṭhabāṇijyam, also 26;.

(m.? to next; cf. Pali paṭikkosana), rejection, scorn, disregard: ˚śena (prose; refers to action of, see next); rejection of, opposition to, action in the saṃgha, In (vs) reads sukhito pramuditaḥ pratikrośaṃ pratilabhati purimanirodhadṛṣṭaṃ, and interprets prati˚ as [Page362-a] referring to the contempt and ill-treatment which pious men will accept with joy in the time of decadence of religion; but this does not seem a natural interpretation, and the mss. read, one, prītiḥ krośaṃ, the other pratikośaṃ; combining parts of each we would get prītikośaṃ, a treasure-store of joy, which makes good sense and which I would read. The meter is very puzzling to me in this whole passage, so that I cannot rely on it.

(= Pali paṭikkosati; cf. prec. and ˚kruṣṭa; if the latter is hyper-Skt., then ˚krośati would seem to be based on ˚kruṣṭa), rejects, scorns, treats with contempt: (yaḥ śāsanaṃ hy arhatāṃ …) ˚śati (= Pali paṭikkosati); (imāṃ prajñāpāramitāṃ …) pratikrokṣyanti (fut.); so also ˚śanti; in (vs) read, yā mamāṇā(ṃ) pratikrośe (aor.), who has scorned (disobeyed) my command; rejects, opposes action in the saṃgha: prativahanti ˚śanti.
(m.?), loss, ruin, disappearance: saddharma-pratikṣayāntakāle (prose); suggest a Pkt. *paḍikkhaya for parikkhaya = Skt. parikṣaya, cf..
, m. (to Skt. ˚kṣipati), one who rejects, contemns: saddharma-pra˚;.

, with atyayaṃ (= Pali accayaṃ paṭiggaṇhāti), accepts (confession of) a sin, forgives: atyayaṃ no sugato ˚ṇātu; yuṣmākaṃ dārikā atyayaṃ ˚ṇāmi 12 (both prose); atyayam atyayataḥ pratigṛhṇīṣva; others, see atyaya.
, m., ‘concealer’, one who acts secretly, on the sly: (Tib. sbad pa).
, m. (lit. receiver; in a similar sense in Skt.,, see; Pali paṭiggaha, receiver for scraps and refuse,), bed-pan (acc. to Tib., chol zaṅs): (among utensils of monks).
, m. (= Pali paṭiggahetā,, cited as ˚hītā; Skt. ˚hītar; cf. graheti, Chap. 43, s.v. grah 3), one who receives: dharmāṇaṃ ˚tāraṃ (Ānandaṃ);; pāṃśukūlānāṃ ˚tāro.
, m., one who took or has taken:, see.
, ppp. (of ‘caus.’, AMg. paḍiggāhia, received, to ˚ggāhei), received, in a-pratigrāhita-bhuktiḥ, eating what has not been received (as a gift):.

, generally m., in nt. (Pali paṭigha, acc. to m. and nt.; Skt. pratigha, m., resistance; [Lex. and a few doubtful literary occurrences] anger), aversion, repugnance, loathing, hostility (hardly anger, at least I find no clear proof for this mg.; but in, where it follows and seems to contrast with rāgaḥ, Tib. renders khon khro ba, anger). It is often bracketed and contrasted with anunaya, q.v. for citations; both (= rāga and dveṣa) are evil and must be shunned. it is called pratigha because it destroys, pratihanti, roots of merit. One of six kleśa, (follows rāgaḥ). Other occurrences (without anunaya):;;;;;;;. See also next.

, m. (= Pali paṭi˚; substantially = prec., but not standardly associated with anunaya; see however, under anunaya), malice, hatred; seems to be contrasted with maitrī: apratighāta-maitrī- (a dvandva), non-malice and kindliness; pratighātaṃ na janayet, maitracittaḥ sadā bhavet;;.
(m.; = Pali paṭicāra; Skt. not in this mg.), dealing with, having relations with: kalyāṇamitropāya-saṃdhi-(q.v.)-lokānuvartana-praticāreṣu. See also prāticāraka (read prati˚?).

, adj. (to prec.), practising, dealing, behaving: anudharma-˚rī, acc. to Tib. behaving according to the dharma (but perh. practising the anudharma, q.v.?); apratihatamatigati-(acc. to, read gatimati- with Tib. and Chin.)- praticāriṇām.
(= Pali paṭicāleti,, cited as ˚caleti), causes to budge or stir, move: śakyo nāhaṃ … drumāt praticālitum (vs).
, investigates, studies carefully: parivartān vibhāvayāmi ˚nomi (prose); perh. error for pravicinomi.

(= Pali paṭicodeti, in this mg. rather than blame, reprove, as given in; even Skt. may have this mg. in, s.v.), countermands, forbids: gdve., a-praticodya-(so to be read, as cpd. with next)-pratijñā-vaiśāradya-prāpta(-tvāt), not to be countermanded or interfered with.
(= Pali paṭi˚, Skt. pratī˚), receives etc.: ppp. praticchita, see; Chap. 43, s.v. iṣ.
(= Pali paṭi˚), covering, in probably Bhvr. cpd. (but possibly adj.): svaka-mukha-pratichādā tasya jihvā prabhūtā.

, nt., ˚na-tā, ˚nā? (in mg. 1, concealment, once in Skt.,), (1) covering, for protection: citta-nagara-prati˚; concealment, gambhīrārtha-dharma-˚na-tā; esp. concealment of oneʼs own faults, duṣṭhula-˚nam; svadoṣa- (text ˚dauṣa-)-˚na-tā; kukṛta-˚na-tā (v.l. ˚nā); (2) (= Pali kaṇḍu-paṭicchādī, f.,, glossed paṭicchādanatthāya) a cloth covering or bandage, in kaṇḍu-˚nam, itch-covering, allowed to monks afflicted with a skin disease:;; spelled kaṇḍū-pratichadanam (Index ˚chād˚, but ˚chad˚).

(m.c. for ˚jāneti, see Chap. 43, s.v. jñā 2, = Skt. ˚jānāti), approves: yādṛśīṃ (what noun is understood?) pratijaneti sūrata eva (= evam) yūyam anuśikṣatho sadā (vs), whatever the Gracious One approves, thus do ye imitate it always.

(also paṭi˚; forms, see Chap. 43; the verb seems to be Vedic only, but a few Skt. noun derivs. are recorded; Pali paṭijaggati, defined in nourish, tend, feed, look after etc., hardly covering the Pali range of mg.), (1) watches = stays awake (opp. sleeps): devī … pratijāgaritvā (vs); (2) watches = guards: yāmaṃ ˚jāgreta (= Pali paṭijaggeyya,; the real meaning of yāma is obscure in both, but prob. lit. night-watch, with thought of mg. 1 preceding; acc. to the three ages of man), not to be em. with ed. (˚jāgṛyāt unmetrical!); kṛtyaṃ ˚jāgareta (oneʼs own acts); here, perhaps, kuśalapakṣaṃ (q.v.) ˚jāgṛhi, etc.; (3) attends to, looks after: ˚jāgaranti (apsarases … the toilet operations of the Bodhisattvaʼs mother); (amātyehi) ˚jāgṛtaṃ, the ministers attended to, carried out (sc. what the king had commanded); yadā ekamātraṃ ˚jāgarti, tadā saptamātrāḥ saṃpadyante (preceded by: sā yadaikaṃ vastu rakṣati tat saptaguṇaṃ syāt: perhaps rather with mg. 2, guards; but it may well be attends to a job); (4) prepares (food): ˚jāgaritvā; (with mss. ˚jāgarayetvā, to caus., or ˚jāgaritvā); ˚jāgrāhi (impv., to ˚jāgrati) (bhaktaṃ);;;; (food and entertainment); (bhojanaṃ);; (5) fixes up, decorates, adorns (orig. prepares, for a festive event), a place: yathājñaptāni sthānāni yathoktaṃ pratijāgriṣu (vs), so read with v.l. for text pari-jā˚, unless MIndic paṭi-jā˚ was the orig. reading, cf. (this might account for pari˚ [Page363-a] of some mss.);; esp. of a road, way (usually mārga) over which a distinguished person is to pass, pratijāgratha (impv.), prepare, adorn, decorate,; ˚jāgaretha (opt.); ˚jāgariṣyāmaḥ; ppp. ˚jāgṛta- (amātyehi ca sarvaṃ ˚jāgṛtaṃ yathā āṇattaṃ; could belong to 3 above, like, but the kingʼs command was to adorn the road); (amātyehi … sarvaṃ ˚jāgṛtaṃ mahatā samṛddhīye pratyudgamanaṃ kṛtaṃ; situation like prec.); devehi mārgo ˚jāgṛto; ˚jāgritaṃ;; mārgaṃ ˚jāgraṃsu (v.l. ˚jāgṛsuḥ;); in some form of this verb seems to be intended, (daśakrośamārgaṃ) pratijāgṛhansuḥ (, almost as one ms. which has ˚jagṛhansuḥ; v.l. pratigrahetsuḥ); suggests contamination with prati-grah-, but this hardly makes sense; what was done is shown by the following (they made the road level, clean, adorned, etc., for the Buddha Dīpaṃkara to pass over).
, adj. (to prec. plus -aka), attending to, in charge of: prahāṇa-˚ko bhikṣuḥ.

(= Pali paṭiññā, ifc. Bhvr. -paṭiñña, in samaṇa-pa˚ … brahmacāri-pa˚, same phrase as below), claim, profession (to be something, with implication of falseness and presumption; cf. Skt. jñā with prati in, mg. 4), only noted in comp., pratijñā-bhikṣu, a monk by (his own) claim (only), Tib. here and below khas ḥche ba, promise with the mouth; otherwise only at end of cpds., esp. in cliché (as in Pali above) aśramaṇaḥ śramaṇapratijñaḥ, abrahmacārī brahmacāripratijñaḥ and (text ˚cārī-prati˚, both edd.; ˚pratijñāḥ both times, as if pl.!);;; plural thruout, same phrase,; ṣaṭ śāstṛpratijñāḥ, the six false, self-alleged teachers, Pūraṇa (q.v.) etc.,; ṣaṭ śāstāra-pratijñā(ḥ) (id.); gen. ṣaṇṇāṃ śāstārapratijñānāṃ 17.
, m., sc. vinaya, or in nt. with karman (= Pali paṭiññāta-karaṇaṃ,, with description, cf. s.v. paṭiññāto), (procedure) which effects confession (of the erring one), one of the 7 adhikaraṇa-śamatha:;.

, adj. (pratijñā-ut˚?),, perh. surpassing oneʼs promise; exceeding expectations; context indicates something like zealous, energetic. Tib. kha ḥog tu lus ḥkhrus pa, bathing the body with face downward (!); but Chin. bathing the body with lower part covered, that is, observing propriety even when alone (a famous Confucian precept).
, beats in return: tāḍito na ˚ḍayati;; tāḍitaḥ ˚ḍayati; tāḍitena (˚tayā) na ˚ḍitavyam;.
, nt., key: = Tib. lde mig. Cf. tālaka.
(virtually = Skt. id.), bases oneself on, relies on (loc.;; believes in, acc. to, = depends on, or accepts as real): (see nimitta 1); cf. upāyakauśalya (uninflected stem form?) pratiṣṭhihitvā (?).
, adj. (= the usual pradakṣiṇa), with karoti, (makes so as to be) on the right hand: praṇamya pādau pratidakṣiṇaṃ ca kṛtvaiva māṃ tasthur ihāgrato me (vs). (No v.l. for prati˚.)
(= pratideśayati, q.v.), confesses: sarvaṃ pratidiśāmy agham = (vs; m.c.?).
